rule.report: content descendants must be in the namespaces 'http://relaxng.org/ns/compatibility/annotations/1.0', 'http://relaxng.org/ns/structure/1.0', 'http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0'
datatype descendants must be in the namespaces 'http://relaxng.org/ns/structure/1.0', 'http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0'

attribute.name: anchored
attribute.a:documentation: (anchored) indicates whether the copy text shows the exact place of reference for the note.

attribute.name: targetEnd
attribute.a:documentation: (target end) points to the end of the span to which the note is attached, if the note is not embedded in the text at that point.

attribute.name: who
attribute.a:documentation: indicates the person, or group of people, to whom the element content is ascribed.

attribute.name: break
attribute.a:documentation: indicates whether or not the element bearing this attribute should be considered to mark the end of an orthographic token in the same way as whitespace.

attribute.name: cRef
attribute.a:documentation: (canonical reference) specifies the destination of the pointer by supplying a canonical reference expressed using the scheme defined in a <refsDecl> element in the TEI header.

attribute.name: key
attribute.a:documentation: provides an externally-defined means of identifying the entity (or entities) being named, using a coded value of some kind.

attribute.name: ref
attribute.a:documentation: (reference) provides an explicit means of locating a full definition or identity for the entity being named by means of one or more URIs.

attribute.name: unit
attribute.a:documentation: identifies the unit of information conveyed by the element. Suggested values include: 1] volume (volume); 2] issue; 3] page (page); 4] line; 5] chapter (chapter); 6] part; 7] column; 8] entry

choice.a:documentation: (volume) the element contains a volume number.
the element contains an issue number, or volume and issue numbers.
(page) the element contains a page number or page range.
the element contains a line number or line range.
(chapter) the element contains a chapter indication (number and/or title)
the element identifies a part of a book or collection.
the element identifies a column.
the element identifies an entry number or label in a list of entries.

attribute.name: from
attribute.a:documentation: specifies the starting point of the range of units indicated by the @unit attribute.

attribute.name: to
attribute.a:documentation: specifies the end-point of the range of units indicated by the @unit attribute.

attribute.name: generatedBy
attribute.a:documentation: (generated by) categorizes how the content of an element was generated in a CMC environment. Suggested values include: 1] human; 2] template; 3] system; 4] bot; 5] unspecified

choice.a:documentation: the content was naturally typed or spoken by a human user
the content was generated after a human user activated a template for its insertion
the content was generated by the system, i.e. the CMC environment
the content was generated by a bot, i.e. a non-human agent, typically one that is not part of the CMC environment itself
the content was generated by an unknown or unspecified process

sch:rule.sch:assert: The @generatedBy attribute is for use within a <post> element.

attribute.name: when
attribute.a:documentation: supplies the value of the date or time in a standard form, e.g. yyyy-mm-dd.

attribute.name: notBefore
attribute.a:documentation: specifies the earliest possible date for the event in standard form, e.g. yyyy-mm-dd.

attribute.name: notAfter
attribute.a:documentation: specifies the latest possible date for the event in standard form, e.g. yyyy-mm-dd.

attribute.name: from
attribute.a:documentation: indicates the starting point of the period in standard form, e.g. yyyy-mm-dd.

attribute.name: to
attribute.a:documentation: indicates the ending point of the period in standard form, e.g. yyyy-mm-dd.

sch:rule.sch:report: The @when attribute cannot be used with any other att.datable.w3c attributes.
The @from and @notBefore attributes cannot be used together.
The @to and @notAfter attributes cannot be used together.

attribute.name: datcat
attribute.a:documentation: provides a pointer to a definition of, and/or general information about, (a) an information container (element or attribute) or (b) a value of an information container (element content or attribute value), by referencing an external taxonomy or ontology. If @valueDatcat is present in the immediate context, this attribute takes on role (a), while @valueDatcat performs role (b).

attribute.name: valueDatcat
attribute.a:documentation: provides a definition of, and/or general information about a value of an information container (element content or attribute value), by reference to an external taxonomy or ontology. Used especially where a contrast with @datcat is needed.

attribute.name: targetDatcat
attribute.a:documentation: provides a definition of, and/or general information about, information structure of an object referenced or modeled by the containing element, by reference to an external taxonomy or ontology. This attribute has the characteristics of the @datcat attribute, except that it addresses not its containing element, but an object that is being referenced or modeled by its containing element.

attribute.name: default
attribute.a:documentation: indicates whether or not this element is selected by default when its parent is selected.

choice.a:documentation: This element is selected if its parent is selected
This element can only be selected explicitly, unless it is the only one of its kind, in which case it is selected if its parent is selected.

attribute.name: decls
attribute.a:documentation: (declarations) identifies one or more declarable elements within the header, which are understood to apply to the element bearing this attribute and its content.

attribute.name: status
attribute.a:documentation: describes the status of a document either currently or, when associated with a dated element, at the time indicated. Sample values include: 1] approved; 2] candidate; 3] cleared; 4] deprecated; 5] draft; 6] embargoed; 7] expired; 8] frozen; 9] galley; 10] proposed; 11] published; 12] recommendation; 13] submitted; 14] unfinished; 15] withdrawn

attribute.name: dur
attribute.a:documentation: (duration) indicates the length of this element in time.

attribute.name: evidence
attribute.a:documentation: indicates the nature of the evidence supporting the reliability or accuracy of the intervention or interpretation. Suggested values include: 1] internal; 2] external; 3] conjecture

choice.a:documentation: there is internal evidence to support the intervention.
there is external evidence to support the intervention.
the intervention or interpretation has been made by the editor, cataloguer, or scholar on the basis of their expertise.

attribute.name: instant
attribute.a:documentation: indicates whether this is an instant revision or not.

attribute.name: ed
attribute.a:documentation: (edition) supplies a sigil or other arbitrary identifier for the source edition in which the associated feature (for example, a page, column, or line beginning) occurs at this point in the text.

attribute.name: edRef
attribute.a:documentation: (edition reference) provides a pointer to the source edition in which the associated feature (for example, a page, column, or line beginning) occurs at this point in the text.

attribute.name: part
attribute.a:documentation: specifies whether or not its parent element is fragmented in some way, typically by some other overlapping structure: for example a speech which is divided between two or more verse stanzas, a paragraph which is split across a page division, a verse line which is divided between two speakers.

choice.a:documentation: (yes) the element is fragmented in some (unspecified) respect
(no) the element is not fragmented, or no claim is made as to its completeness
(initial) this is the initial part of a fragmented element
(medial) this is a medial part of a fragmented element
(final) this is the final part of a fragmented element

attribute.name: rend
attribute.a:documentation: (rendition) indicates how the element in question was rendered or presented in the source text.

attribute.name: style
attribute.a:documentation: contains an expression in some formal style definition language which defines the rendering or presentation used for this element in the source text.

attribute.name: rendition
attribute.a:documentation: (rendition reference) points to a description of the rendering or presentation used for this element in the source text.

attribute.name: cert
attribute.a:documentation: (certainty) signifies the degree of certainty associated with the intervention or interpretation.

attribute.name: resp
attribute.a:documentation: (responsible party) indicates the agency responsible for the intervention or interpretation, for example an editor or transcriber.

attribute.name: source
attribute.a:documentation: specifies the source from which some aspect of this element is drawn.

sch:report.test: ( self::tei:classRef | self::tei:dataRef | self::tei:elementRef | self::tei:macroRef | self::tei:moduleRef | self::tei:schemaSpec ) and $srcs[2]

sch:rule.sch:report: When used on a schema description element (like <>), the @source attribute should have only 1 value. (This one has .)

attribute.name: indentLevel
attribute.a:documentation: specifies the level of indentation of an item using a numeric value.

attribute.name: mimeType
attribute.a:documentation: (MIME media type) specifies the applicable multimedia internet mail extension (MIME) media type.

attribute.name: type
attribute.a:documentation: indicates what kind of phenomenon is being noted in the passage. Sample values include: 1] image; 2] character; 3] theme; 4] allusion

attribute.name: subtype
attribute.a:documentation: (subtype) provides a sub-categorization of the phenomenon is being noted in the passage, if needed.

attribute.name: inst
attribute.a:documentation: (instances) points to instances of the analysis or interpretation represented by the current element.

attribute.name: unit
attribute.a:documentation: (unit) indicates the units used for the measurement, usually using the standard symbol for the desired units. Suggested values include: 1] m (metre); 2] kg (kilogram); 3] s (second); 4] Hz (hertz); 5] Pa (pascal); 6] Ω (ohm); 7] L (litre); 8] t (tonne); 9] ha (hectare); 10] Å (ångström); 11] mL (millilitre); 12] cm (centimetre); 13] dB (decibel); 14] kbit (kilobit); 15] Kibit (kibibit); 16] kB (kilobyte); 17] KiB (kibibyte); 18] MB (megabyte); 19] MiB (mebibyte)

choice.a:documentation: (metre) SI base unit of length
(kilogram) SI base unit of mass
(second) SI base unit of time
(hertz) SI unit of frequency
(pascal) SI unit of pressure or stress
(ohm) SI unit of electric resistance
(litre) 1 dm³
(tonne) 10³ kg
(hectare) 1 hm²
(ångström) 10⁻¹⁰ m
(millilitre)
(centimetre)
(decibel) see remarks, below
(kilobit) 10³ or 1000 bits
(kibibit) 2¹⁰ or 1024 bits
(kilobyte) 10³ or 1000 bytes
(kibibyte) 2¹⁰ or 1024 bytes
(megabyte) 10⁶ or 1 000 000 bytes
(mebibyte) 2²⁰ or 1 048 576 bytes

attribute.name: unitRef
attribute.a:documentation: points to a unique identifier stored in the @xml:id of a <unitDef> element that defines a unit of measure.

attribute.name: quantity
attribute.a:documentation: (quantity) specifies the number of the specified units that comprise the measurement

attribute.name: commodity
attribute.a:documentation: (commodity) indicates the substance that is being measured

attribute.name: notation
attribute.a:documentation: names the notation used for the content of the element.

attribute.name: place
attribute.a:documentation: specifies where this item is placed. Suggested values include: 1] top; 2] bottom; 3] margin; 4] opposite; 5] overleaf; 6] above; 7] right; 8] below; 9] left; 10] end; 11] inline; 12] inspace

choice.a:documentation: at the top of the page
at the foot of the page
in the margin (left, right, or both)
on the opposite, i.e. facing, page
on the other side of the leaf
above the line
to the right, e.g. to the right of a vertical line of text, or to the right of a figure
below the line
to the left, e.g. to the left of a vertical line of text, or to the left of a figure
at the end of e.g. chapter or volume.
within the body of the text.
in a predefined space, for example left by an earlier scribe.

attribute.name: targetLang
attribute.a:documentation: specifies the language of the content to be found at the destination referenced by @target, using a language tag generated according to BCP 47.

sch:rule.sch:assert: @targetLang should only be used on <> if @target is specified.

rng:attribute.name: target
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the destination of the reference by supplying one or more URI References.

rng:attribute.name: evaluate
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (evaluate) specifies the intended meaning when the target of a pointer is itself a pointer.

rng:choice.a:documentation: if the element pointed to is itself a pointer, then the target of that pointer will be taken, and so on, until an element is found which is not a pointer.
if the element pointed to is itself a pointer, then its target (whether a pointer or not) is taken as the target of this pointer.
no further evaluation of targets is carried out beyond that needed to find the element specified in the pointer's target.

rng:attribute.name: atLeast
rng:attribute.a:documentation: gives a minimum estimated value for the approximate measurement.

rng:attribute.name: atMost
rng:attribute.a:documentation: gives a maximum estimated value for the approximate measurement.

rng:attribute.name: min
rng:attribute.a:documentation: where the measurement summarizes more than one observation or a range, supplies the minimum value observed.

rng:attribute.name: max
rng:attribute.a:documentation: where the measurement summarizes more than one observation or a range, supplies the maximum value observed.

rng:attribute.name: confidence
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the degree of statistical confidence (between zero and one) that a value falls within the range specified by @min and @max, or the proportion of observed values that fall within that range.

rng:attribute.name: url
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (uniform resource locator) specifies the URL from which the media concerned may be obtained.

rng:attribute.name: scope
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates the scope of application of the element Suggested values include: 1] sole; 2] major; 3] minor

rng:choice.a:documentation: only this particular feature is used throughout the document
this feature is used through most of the document
this feature is used occasionally through the document

rng:attribute.name: target
rng:attribute.a:documentation: points at one or more sets of zero or more elements each.

rng:attribute.name: match
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies an XPath selection pattern using the syntax defined in which identifies a set of nodes, selected within the context identified by the @target attribute if this is supplied, or within the context of the parent element if it is not.

rng:attribute.name: sortKey
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies the sort key for this element in an index, list or group which contains it.

rng:attribute.name: spanTo
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates the end of a span initiated by the element bearing this attribute.

sch:rule.sch:assert: The element indicated by @spanTo () must follow the current <> element.

rng:attribute.name: scheme
rng:attribute.a:documentation: identifies the language used to describe the rendition.

rng:choice.a:documentation: Cascading Stylesheet Language
Extensible Stylesheet Language Formatting Objects
Informal free text description
A user-defined rendition description language

rng:attribute.name: schemeVersion
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies a version number for the style language provided in @scheme.

sch:rule.sch:assert: @schemeVersion can only be used if @scheme is specified.

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: characterizes the element in some sense, using any convenient classification scheme or typology.

rng:attribute.name: subtype
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (subtype) provides a sub-categorization of the element, if needed.

sch:rule.sch:assert: The <> element should not be categorized in detail with @subtype unless also categorized in general with @type.

rng:attribute.name: hand
rng:attribute.a:documentation: points to a <handNote> element describing the hand considered responsible for the content of the element concerned.

rng:attribute.name: toWhom
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates the person, or group of people, to whom a speech act or action is directed.

rng:attribute.name: period
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies pointers to one or more definitions of named periods of time (typically <category>s, <date>s, or <event>s) within which the datable item is understood to have occurred.

rng:attribute.name: unit
rng:attribute.a:documentation: names the unit used for the measurement Suggested values include: 1] cm (centimetres); 2] mm (millimetres); 3] in (inches); 4] line; 5] char (characters)

rng:choice.a:documentation: (centimetres)
(millimetres)
(inches)
lines of text
(characters) characters of text

rng:attribute.name: quantity
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the length in the units specified

rng:attribute.name: extent
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates the size of the object concerned using a project-specific vocabulary combining quantity and units in a single string of words.

rng:attribute.name: precision
rng:attribute.a:documentation: characterizes the precision of the values specified by the other attributes.

rng:attribute.name: scope
rng:attribute.a:documentation: where the measurement summarizes more than one observation, specifies the applicability of this measurement. Sample values include: 1] all; 2] most; 3] range

rng:attribute.name: org
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (organization) specifies how the content of the division is organized.

rng:choice.a:documentation: no claim is made about the sequence in which the immediate contents of this division are to be processed, or their inter-relationships.
the contents of this element are intended to represent simultaneous or side-by-side delivery.
the immediate contents of this element are regarded as forming a logical unit, to be processed in sequence.

rng:attribute.name: sample
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates whether this division is a sample of the original source and if so, from which part.

rng:choice.a:documentation: division lacks material present at end in source.
division lacks material at start and end.
division lacks material at start.
position of sampled material within original unknown.
division is not a sample.

rng:attribute.name: xml:id
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (identifier) provides a unique identifier for the element bearing the attribute.

rng:attribute.name: n
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (number) gives a number (or other label) for an element, which is not necessarily unique within the document.

rng:attribute.name: xml:lang
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (language) indicates the language of the element content using a tag generated according to BCP 47.

rng:attribute.name: xml:base
rng:attribute.a:documentation: provides a base URI reference with which applications can resolve relative URI references into absolute URI references.

rng:attribute.name: xml:space
rng:attribute.a:documentation: signals an intention about how white space should be managed by applications.

rng:choice.a:documentation: signals that the application's default white-space processing modes are acceptable
indicates the intent that applications preserve all white space

rng:attribute.name: scribe
rng:attribute.a:documentation: gives a name or other identifier for the scribe believed to be responsible for this hand.

rng:attribute.name: scribeRef
rng:attribute.a:documentation: points to a full description of the scribe concerned, typically supplied by a <person> element elsewhere in the description.

rng:attribute.name: script
rng:attribute.a:documentation: characterizes the particular script or writing style used by this hand, for example secretary, copperplate, Chancery, Italian, etc.

rng:attribute.name: scriptRef
rng:attribute.a:documentation: points to a full description of the script or writing style used by this hand, typically supplied by a <scriptNote> element elsewhere in the description.

rng:attribute.name: medium
rng:attribute.a:documentation: describes the tint or type of ink, e.g. brown, or other writing medium, e.g. pencil.

rng:attribute.name: width
rng:attribute.a:documentation: Where the media are displayed, indicates the display width.

rng:attribute.name: height
rng:attribute.a:documentation: Where the media are displayed, indicates the display height.

rng:attribute.name: scale
rng:attribute.a:documentation: Where the media are displayed, indicates a scale factor to be applied when generating the desired display size.

rng:attribute.name: role
rng:attribute.a:documentation: may be used to specify further information about the entity referenced by this name in the form of a set of whitespace-separated values, for example the occupation of a person, or the status of a place.

rng:attribute.name: nymRef
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (reference to the canonical name) provides a means of locating the canonical form (nym) of the names associated with the object named by the element bearing it.

rng:attribute.name: domains
rng:attribute.a:documentation: optionally specifies the identifiers of the elements within which all elements indicated by the contents of this element lie.

rng:attribute.name: targFunc
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (target function) describes the function of each of the values of the @target attribute of the enclosed <link>, <join>, or <alt> tags.

rng:attribute.name: function
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (function) characterizes the function of the segment.

rng:attribute.name: status
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates the effect of the intervention, for example in the case of a deletion, strikeouts which include too much or too little text, or in the case of an addition, an insertion which duplicates some of the text already present. Sample values include: 1] duplicate; 2] duplicate-partial; 3] excessStart; 4] excessEnd; 5] shortStart; 6] shortEnd; 7] partial; 8] unremarkable

rng:attribute.name: cause
rng:attribute.a:documentation: documents the presumed cause for the intervention.

rng:attribute.name: seq
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (sequence) assigns a sequence number related to the order in which the encoded features carrying this attribute are believed to have occurred.

rng:attribute.name: agent
rng:attribute.a:documentation: categorizes the cause of the damage, if it can be identified. Sample values include: 1] rubbing; 2] mildew; 3] smoke

rng:attribute.name: degree
rng:attribute.a:documentation: provides a coded representation of the degree of damage, either as a number between 0 (undamaged) and 1 (very extensively damaged), or as one of the codes high, medium, low, or unknown. The <damage> element with the @degree attribute should only be used where the text may be read with some confidence; text supplied from other sources should be tagged as <supplied>.

rng:attribute.name: group
rng:attribute.a:documentation: assigns an arbitrary number to each stretch of damage regarded as forming part of the same physical phenomenon.

rng:attribute.name: start
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates the location within a temporal alignment at which this element begins.

rng:attribute.name: end
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates the location within a temporal alignment at which this element ends.

rng:attribute.name: formula
rng:attribute.a:documentation: A @formula is provided to describe a mathematical calculation such as a conversion between measurement systems.

rng:attribute.name: where
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates one or more locations by pointing to a <place> element or other canonical description.

rng:attribute.name: extent
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates whether the pronunciation or orthography applies to all or part of a word. Suggested values include: 1] full (full form); 2] pref (prefix); 3] suff (suffix); 4] inf (infix); 5] part (partial)

rng:choice.a:documentation: (full form)
(prefix)
(suffix)
(infix)
(partial)

rng:attribute.name: full
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates whether the name component is given in full, as an abbreviation or simply as an initial.

rng:choice.a:documentation: (yes) the name component is spelled out in full.
(abbreviated) the name component is given in an abbreviated form.
(initial letter) the name component is indicated only by one initial.

rng:attribute.name: sort
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (sort) specifies the sort order of the name component in relation to others within the name.

rng:attribute.name: calendar
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates one or more systems or calendars to which the date represented by the content of this element belongs.

rng:attribute.name: dur-iso
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (duration) indicates the length of this element in time.

rng:attribute.name: unit
rng:attribute.a:documentation: provides a conventional name for the kind of section changing at this milestone. Suggested values include: 1] page; 2] column; 3] line; 4] book; 5] poem; 6] canto; 7] speaker; 8] stanza; 9] act; 10] scene; 11] section; 12] absent; 13] unnumbered

rng:choice.a:documentation: physical page beginnings (synonymous with the <pb> element).
column beginnings.
line beginnings (synonymous with the <lb> element).
any units termed book, liber, etc.
individual poems in a collection.
cantos or other major sections of a poem.
changes of speaker or narrator.
stanzas within a poem, book, or canto.
acts within a play.
scenes within a play or act.
sections of any kind.
passages not present in the reference edition.
passages present in the text, but not to be included as part of the reference.

rng:element.name: p
rng:element.a:documentation: (paragraph) marks paragraphs in prose. [3.1. Paragraphs 7.2.6. Speech Contents]
