rng:element.name: foreign
rng:element.a:documentation: (foreign) identifies a word or phrase as belonging to some language other than that of the surrounding text. [3.3.2.1. Foreign Words or Expressions]

rng:element.name: emph
rng:element.a:documentation: (emphasized) marks words or phrases which are stressed or emphasized for linguistic or rhetorical effect. [3.3.2.2. Emphatic Words and Phrases 3.3.2. Emphasis, Foreign Words, and Unusual Language]

rng:element.name: hi
rng:element.a:documentation: (highlighted) marks a word or phrase as graphically distinct from the surrounding text, for reasons concerning which no claim is made. [3.3.2.2. Emphatic Words and Phrases 3.3.2. Emphasis, Foreign Words, and Unusual Language]

rng:element.name: distinct
rng:element.a:documentation: identifies any word or phrase which is regarded as linguistically distinct, for example as archaic, technical, dialectal, non-preferred, etc., or as forming part of a sublanguage. [3.3.2.3. Other Linguistically Distinct Material]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the sublanguage or register to which the word or phrase is being assigned.

rng:attribute.name: time
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies how the phrase is distinct diachronically.

rng:attribute.name: space
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies how the phrase is distinct diatopically.

rng:attribute.name: social
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies how the phrase is distinct diastratically.

rng:element.name: said
rng:element.a:documentation: (speech or thought) indicates passages thought or spoken aloud, whether explicitly indicated in the source or not, whether directly or indirectly reported, whether by real people or fictional characters. [3.3.3. Quotation]

rng:attribute.name: aloud
rng:attribute.a:documentation: may be used to indicate whether the quoted matter is regarded as having been vocalized or signed.

rng:attribute.name: direct
rng:attribute.a:documentation: may be used to indicate whether the quoted matter is regarded as direct or indirect speech.

rng:element.name: quote
rng:element.a:documentation: (quotation) contains a phrase or passage attributed by the narrator or author to some agency external to the text. [3.3.3. Quotation 4.3.1. Grouped Texts]

rng:element.name: q
rng:element.a:documentation: (quoted) contains material which is distinguished from the surrounding text using quotation marks or a similar method, for any one of a variety of reasons including, but not limited to: direct speech or thought, technical terms or jargon, authorial distance, quotations from elsewhere, and passages that are mentioned but not used. [3.3.3. Quotation]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (type) may be used to indicate whether the offset passage is spoken or thought, or to characterize it more finely. Suggested values include: 1] spoken (spoken); 2] thought (thought); 3] written (written); 4] soCalled (so called); 5] foreign (foreign); 6] distinct (distinct); 7] term; 8] emph (emph); 9] mentioned (mentioned)

rng:choice.a:documentation: (spoken) representation of speech
(thought) representation of thought, e.g. internal monologue
(written) quotation from a written source
(so called) authorial distance
(foreign) foreign words
(distinct) linguistically distinct
technical term
(emph) rhetorically emphasized
(mentioned) refering to itself, not its normal referent

rng:element.name: cit
rng:element.a:documentation: (cited quotation) contains a quotation from some other document, together with a bibliographic reference to its source. In a dictionary it may contain an example text with at least one occurrence of the word form, used in the sense being described, or a translation of the headword, or an example. [3.3.3. Quotation 4.3.1. Grouped Texts 10.3.5.1. Examples]

rng:element.name: mentioned
rng:element.a:documentation: marks words or phrases mentioned, not used. [3.3.3. Quotation]

rng:element.name: soCalled
rng:element.a:documentation: (so called) contains a word or phrase for which the author or narrator indicates a disclaiming of responsibility, for example by the use of scare quotes or italics. [3.3.3. Quotation]

rng:element.name: desc
rng:element.a:documentation: (description) contains a short description of the purpose, function, or use of its parent element, or when the parent is a documentation element, describes or defines the object being documented. [23.4.1. Description of Components]

sch:rule.sch:assert: Information about a deprecation should only be present in a specification element that is being deprecated: that is, only an element that has a @validUntil attribute should have a child <desc type="deprecationInfo">.

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: characterizes the element in some sense, using any convenient classification scheme or typology. Suggested values include: 1] deprecationInfo (deprecation information)

rng:choice.a:documentation: (deprecation information) This element describes why or how its parent element is being deprecated, typically including recommendations for alternate encoding.

rng:element.name: gloss
rng:element.a:documentation: (gloss) identifies a phrase or word used to provide a gloss or definition for some other word or phrase. [3.4.1. Terms and Glosses 23.4.1. Description of Components]

rng:element.name: term
rng:element.a:documentation: (term) contains a single-word, multi-word, or symbolic designation which is regarded as a technical term. [3.4.1. Terms and Glosses]

rng:element.name: ruby
rng:element.a:documentation: (ruby container) contains a passage of base text along with its associated ruby gloss(es). [3.4.2. Ruby Annotations]

rng:element.name: rb
rng:element.a:documentation: (ruby base) contains the base text annotated by a ruby gloss. [3.4.2. Ruby Annotations]

rng:element.name: rt
rng:element.a:documentation: (ruby text) contains a ruby text, an annotation closely associated with a passage of the main text. [3.4.2. Ruby Annotations]

rng:attribute.name: target
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies a pointer to the base being glossed by this ruby text.

sch:rule.sch:report: When @target is present, neither @from nor @to should be.

rng:attribute.name: from
rng:attribute.a:documentation: points to the starting point of the span of text being glossed by this ruby text.

sch:rule.sch:assert: When @from is present, the @to attribute of <> is required.

rng:attribute.name: to
rng:attribute.a:documentation: points to the ending point of the span of text being glossed.

sch:rule.sch:assert: When @to is present, the @from attribute of <> is required.

rng:element.name: sic
rng:element.a:documentation: (Latin for thus or so) contains text reproduced although apparently incorrect or inaccurate. [3.5.1. Apparent Errors]

rng:element.name: corr
rng:element.a:documentation: (correction) contains the correct form of a passage apparently erroneous in the copy text. [3.5.1. Apparent Errors]

rng:element.name: choice
rng:element.a:documentation: (choice) groups a number of alternative encodings for the same point in a text. [3.5. Simple Editorial Changes]

rng:element.name: reg
rng:element.a:documentation: (regularization) contains a reading which has been regularized or normalized in some sense. [3.5.2. Regularization and Normalization 13. Critical Apparatus]

rng:element.name: orig
rng:element.a:documentation: (original form) contains a reading which is marked as following the original, rather than being normalized or corrected. [3.5.2. Regularization and Normalization 13. Critical Apparatus]

rng:element.name: gap
rng:element.a:documentation: (gap) indicates a point where material has been omitted in a transcription, whether for editorial reasons described in the TEI header, as part of sampling practice, or because the material is illegible, invisible, or inaudible. [3.5.3. Additions, Deletions, and Omissions]

rng:attribute.name: reason
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (reason) gives the reason for omission. Suggested values include: 1] cancelled (cancelled); 2] deleted (deleted); 3] editorial (editorial); 4] illegible (illegible); 5] inaudible (inaudible); 6] irrelevant (irrelevant); 7] sampling (sampling)

rng:choice.a:documentation: (cancelled)
(deleted)
(editorial) for features omitted from transcription due to editorial policy
(illegible)
(inaudible)
(irrelevant)
(sampling)

rng:attribute.name: agent
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (agent) in the case of text omitted because of damage, categorizes the cause of the damage, if it can be identified. Sample values include: 1] rubbing (rubbing); 2] mildew (mildew); 3] smoke (smoke)

rng:element.name: ellipsis
rng:element.a:documentation: (deliberately marked omission) indicates a purposeful marking in the source document signalling that content has been omitted, and may also supply or describe the omitted content. [3.5.3. Additions, Deletions, and Omissions]

rng:element.name: add
rng:element.a:documentation: (addition) contains letters, words, or phrases inserted in the source text by an author, scribe, or a previous annotator or corrector. [3.5.3. Additions, Deletions, and Omissions]

rng:element.name: del
rng:element.a:documentation: (deletion) contains a letter, word, or passage deleted, marked as deleted, or otherwise indicated as superfluous or spurious in the copy text by an author, scribe, or a previous annotator or corrector. [3.5.3. Additions, Deletions, and Omissions]

rng:element.name: unclear
rng:element.a:documentation: (unclear) contains a word, phrase, or passage which cannot be transcribed with certainty because it is illegible or inaudible in the source. [12.3.3.1. Damage, Illegibility, and Supplied Text 3.5.3. Additions, Deletions, and Omissions]

rng:attribute.name: reason
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates why the material is hard to transcribe. Suggested values include: 1] illegible (illegible); 2] inaudible (inaudible); 3] faded (faded); 4] background_noise (background noise); 5] eccentric_ductus (eccentric ductus)

rng:choice.a:documentation: (illegible)
(inaudible)
(faded)
(background noise)
(eccentric ductus) indicates illegibility due to an unusual, awkward, or incompetent execution of a glyph or glyphs

rng:attribute.name: agent
rng:attribute.a:documentation: Where the difficulty in transcription arises from damage, categorizes the cause of the damage, if it can be identified. Sample values include: 1] rubbing; 2] mildew; 3] smoke

rng:element.name: name
rng:element.a:documentation: (name, proper noun) contains a proper noun or noun phrase. [3.6.1. Referring Strings]

rng:element.name: rs
rng:element.a:documentation: (referencing string) contains a general purpose name or referring string. [14.2.1. Personal Names 3.6.1. Referring Strings]

rng:element.name: email
rng:element.a:documentation: (electronic mail address) contains an email address identifying a location to which email messages can be delivered. [3.6.2. Addresses]

rng:element.name: address
rng:element.a:documentation: (address) contains a postal address, for example of a publisher, an organization, or an individual. [3.6.2. Addresses 2.2.4. Publication, Distribution, Licensing, etc. 3.12.2.4. Imprint, Size of a Document, and Reprint Information]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: characterizes the address in some sense, using any convenient classification scheme or typology. Suggested values include: 1] billing; 2] delivery; 3] mailing; 4] military; 5] physical

rng:choice.a:documentation: the address to which a bill for goods or services should be sent.
the address to which packages should be sent via a private delivery service.
the address to which mail should be sent via a public postal service.
the address to which mail to deployed military personnel should be sent.
the address of a building irrespective of where mail to its occupants should be sent (for example, for the fire department).

rng:attribute.name: role
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies further information about the purpose of the address. Sample values include: 1] sender; 2] return; 3] recipient ; 4] work; 5] home; 6] start; 7] finish; 8] pickup; 9] dropOff

rng:element.name: addrLine
rng:element.a:documentation: (address line) contains one line of a postal address. [3.6.2. Addresses 2.2.4. Publication, Distribution, Licensing, etc. 3.12.2.4. Imprint, Size of a Document, and Reprint Information]

rng:element.name: street
rng:element.a:documentation: contains a full street address including any name or number identifying a building as well as the name of the street or route on which it is located. [3.6.2. Addresses]

rng:element.name: postCode
rng:element.a:documentation: (postal code) contains a numerical or alphanumeric code used as part of a postal address to simplify sorting or delivery of mail. [3.6.2. Addresses]

rng:element.name: postBox
rng:element.a:documentation: (postal box or post office box) contains a number or other identifier for some postal delivery point other than a street address. [3.6.2. Addresses]

rng:element.name: num
rng:element.a:documentation: (number) contains a number, written in any form. [3.6.3. Numbers and Measures]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates the type of numeric value. Suggested values include: 1] cardinal; 2] ordinal; 3] fraction; 4] percentage

rng:choice.a:documentation: absolute number, e.g. 21, 21.5
ordinal number, e.g. 21st
fraction, e.g. one half or three-quarters
a percentage

rng:attribute.name: value
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies the value of the number in standard form.

rng:element.name: measure
rng:element.a:documentation: (measure) contains a word or phrase referring to some quantity of an object or commodity, usually comprising a number, a unit, and a commodity name. [3.6.3. Numbers and Measures]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the type of measurement in any convenient typology.

rng:element.name: measureGrp
rng:element.a:documentation: (measure group) contains a group of dimensional specifications which relate to the same object, for example the height and width of a manuscript page. [11.3.4. Dimensions]

rng:element.name: unit
rng:element.a:documentation: contains a symbol, a word or a phrase referring to a unit of measurement in any kind of formal or informal system. [3.6.3. Numbers and Measures]

rng:element.name: date
rng:element.a:documentation: (date) contains a date in any format. [3.6.4. Dates and Times 2.2.4. Publication, Distribution, Licensing, etc. 2.6. The Revision Description 3.12.2.4. Imprint, Size of a Document, and Reprint Information 16.2.3. The Setting Description 14.4. Dates]

rng:element.name: time
rng:element.a:documentation: (time) contains a phrase defining a time of day in any format. [3.6.4. Dates and Times]

rng:element.name: abbr
rng:element.a:documentation: (abbreviation) contains an abbreviation of any sort. [3.6.5. Abbreviations and Their Expansions]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (type) allows the encoder to classify the abbreviation according to some convenient typology. Sample values include: 1] suspension (suspension); 2] contraction (contraction); 3] brevigraph; 4] superscription (superscription); 5] acronym (acronym); 6] title (title); 7] organization (organization); 8] geographic (geographic)

rng:element.name: expan
rng:element.a:documentation: (expansion) contains the expansion of an abbreviation. [3.6.5. Abbreviations and Their Expansions]

rng:element.name: ptr
rng:element.a:documentation: (pointer) defines a pointer to another location. [3.7. Simple Links and Cross-References 17.1. Links]

sch:rule.sch:report: Only one of the attributes @target and @cRef may be supplied on <>.

rng:element.name: ref
rng:element.a:documentation: (reference) defines a reference to another location, possibly modified by additional text or comment. [3.7. Simple Links and Cross-References 17.1. Links]

sch:rule.sch:report: Only one of the attributes @target and @cRef may be supplied on <>.

rng:element.name: list
rng:element.a:documentation: (list) contains any sequence of items organized as a list. [3.8. Lists]

sch:rule.sch:assert: The content of a "gloss" list should include a sequence of one or more pairs of a <label> element followed by an <item> element.

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (type) describes the nature of the items in the list. Suggested values include: 1] gloss (gloss); 2] index (index); 3] instructions (instructions); 4] litany (litany); 5] syllogism (syllogism)

rng:choice.a:documentation: (gloss) each list item glosses some term or concept, which is given by a <label> element preceding the list item.
(index) each list item is an entry in an index such as the alphabetical topical index at the back of a print volume.
(instructions) each list item is a step in a sequence of instructions, as in a recipe.
(litany) each list item is one of a sequence of petitions, supplications or invocations, typically in a religious ritual.
(syllogism) each list item is part of an argument consisting of two or more propositions and a final conclusion derived from them.

rng:element.name: item
rng:element.a:documentation: (item) contains one component of a list. [3.8. Lists 2.6. The Revision Description]

rng:element.name: label
rng:element.a:documentation: (label) contains any label or heading used to identify part of a text, typically but not exclusively in a list or glossary. [3.8. Lists]

rng:element.name: head
rng:element.a:documentation: (heading) contains any type of heading, for example the title of a section, or the heading of a list, glossary, manuscript description, etc. [4.2.1. Headings and Trailers]

rng:element.name: headLabel
rng:element.a:documentation: (heading for list labels) contains the heading for the label or term column in a glossary list or similar structured list. [3.8. Lists]

rng:element.name: headItem
rng:element.a:documentation: (heading for list items) contains the heading for the item or gloss column in a glossary list or similar structured list. [3.8. Lists]

rng:element.name: note
rng:element.a:documentation: (note) contains a note or annotation. [3.9.1. Notes and Simple Annotation 2.2.6. The Notes Statement 3.12.2.8. Notes and Statement of Language 10.3.5.4. Notes within Entries]

rng:element.name: noteGrp
rng:element.a:documentation: (note group) contains a group of notes. [3.9.1.1. Encoding Grouped Notes]

rng:element.name: index
rng:element.a:documentation: (index entry) marks a location to be indexed for whatever purpose. [3.9.2. Index Entries]

rng:attribute.name: indexName
rng:attribute.a:documentation: a single word which follows the rules defining a legal XML name (see ), supplying a name to specify which index (of several) the index entry belongs to.

rng:element.name: media
rng:element.a:documentation: indicates the location of any form of external media such as an audio or video clip etc. [3.10. Graphics and Other Non-textual Components]

rng:attribute.name: mimeType
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (MIME media type) specifies the applicable multimedia internet mail extension (MIME) media type.

rng:element.name: graphic
rng:element.a:documentation: (graphic) indicates the location of a graphic or illustration, either forming part of a text, or providing an image of it. [3.10. Graphics and Other Non-textual Components 12.1. Digital Facsimiles]

rng:element.name: binaryObject
rng:element.a:documentation: provides encoded binary data representing an inline graphic, audio, video or other object. [3.10. Graphics and Other Non-textual Components]

rng:attribute.name: encoding
rng:attribute.a:documentation: The encoding used to encode the binary data. If not specified, this is assumed to be Base64.

rng:element.name: milestone
rng:element.a:documentation: (milestone) marks a boundary point separating any kind of section of a text, typically but not necessarily indicating a point at which some part of a standard reference system changes, where the change is not represented by a structural element. [3.11.3. Milestone Elements]

rng:element.name: gb
rng:element.a:documentation: (gathering beginning) marks the beginning of a new gathering or quire in a transcribed codex. [3.11.3. Milestone Elements]

rng:element.name: pb
rng:element.a:documentation: (page beginning) marks the beginning of a new page in a paginated document. [3.11.3. Milestone Elements]

rng:element.name: lb
rng:element.a:documentation: (line beginning) marks the beginning of a topographic line in some edition or version of a text. [3.11.3. Milestone Elements 7.2.6. Speech Contents]

rng:element.name: cb
rng:element.a:documentation: (column beginning) marks the beginning of a new column of a text on a multi-column page. [3.11.3. Milestone Elements]

rng:element.name: analytic
rng:element.a:documentation: (analytic level) contains bibliographic elements describing an item (e.g. an article or poem) published within a monograph or journal and not as an independent publication. [3.12.2.1. Analytic, Monographic, and Series Levels]

rng:element.name: monogr
rng:element.a:documentation: (monographic level) contains bibliographic elements describing an item (e.g. a book or journal) published as an independent item (i.e. as a separate physical object). [3.12.2.1. Analytic, Monographic, and Series Levels]

rng:element.name: series
rng:element.a:documentation: (series information) contains information about the series in which a book or other bibliographic item has appeared. [3.12.2.1. Analytic, Monographic, and Series Levels]

rng:element.name: author
rng:element.a:documentation: (author) in a bibliographic reference, contains the name(s) of an author, personal or corporate, of a work; for example in the same form as that provided by a recognized bibliographic name authority. [3.12.2.2. Titles, Authors, and Editors 2.2.1. The Title Statement]

rng:element.name: editor
rng:element.a:documentation: contains a secondary statement of responsibility for a bibliographic item, for example the name of an individual, institution or organization, (or of several such) acting as editor, compiler, translator, etc. [3.12.2.2. Titles, Authors, and Editors]

rng:element.name: respStmt
rng:element.a:documentation: (statement of responsibility) supplies a statement of responsibility for the intellectual content of a text, edition, recording, or series, where the specialized elements for authors, editors, etc. do not suffice or do not apply. May also be used to encode information about individuals or organizations which have played a role in the production or distribution of a bibliographic work. [3.12.2.2. Titles, Authors, and Editors 2.2.1. The Title Statement 2.2.2. The Edition Statement 2.2.5. The Series Statement]

rng:element.name: resp
rng:element.a:documentation: (responsibility) contains a phrase describing the nature of a person's intellectual responsibility, or an organization's role in the production or distribution of a work. [3.12.2.2. Titles, Authors, and Editors 2.2.1. The Title Statement 2.2.2. The Edition Statement 2.2.5. The Series Statement]

rng:element.name: title
rng:element.a:documentation: (title) contains a title for any kind of work. [3.12.2.2. Titles, Authors, and Editors 2.2.1. The Title Statement 2.2.5. The Series Statement]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: classifies the title according to some convenient typology. Sample values include: 1] main; 2] sub (subordinate); 3] alt (alternate); 4] short; 5] desc (descriptive)

rng:attribute.name: level
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates the bibliographic level for a title, that is, whether it identifies an article, book, journal, series, or unpublished material.

rng:choice.a:documentation: (analytic) the title applies to an analytic item, such as an article, poem, or other work published as part of a larger item.
(monographic) the title applies to a monograph such as a book or other item considered to be a distinct publication, including single volumes of multi-volume works
(journal) the title applies to any serial or periodical publication such as a journal, magazine, or newspaper
(series) the title applies to a series of otherwise distinct publications such as a collection
(unpublished) the title applies to any unpublished material (including theses and dissertations unless published by a commercial press)

rng:element.name: meeting
rng:element.a:documentation: contains the formalized descriptive title for a meeting or conference, for use in a bibliographic description for an item derived from such a meeting, or as a heading or preamble to publications emanating from it. [3.12.2.2. Titles, Authors, and Editors]

rng:element.name: imprint
rng:element.a:documentation: groups information relating to the publication or distribution of a bibliographic item. [3.12.2.4. Imprint, Size of a Document, and Reprint Information]

rng:element.name: publisher
rng:element.a:documentation: (publisher) provides the name of the organization responsible for the publication or distribution of a bibliographic item. [3.12.2.4. Imprint, Size of a Document, and Reprint Information 2.2.4. Publication, Distribution, Licensing, etc.]

rng:element.name: biblScope
rng:element.a:documentation: (scope of bibliographic reference) defines the scope of a bibliographic reference, for example as a list of page numbers, or a named subdivision of a larger work. [3.12.2.5. Scopes and Ranges in Bibliographic Citations]

rng:element.name: citedRange
rng:element.a:documentation: (cited range) defines the range of cited content, often represented by pages or other units. [3.12.2.5. Scopes and Ranges in Bibliographic Citations]

rng:element.name: pubPlace
rng:element.a:documentation: (publication place) contains the name of the place where a bibliographic item was published. [3.12.2.4. Imprint, Size of a Document, and Reprint Information]

rng:element.name: bibl
rng:element.a:documentation: (bibliographic citation) contains a loosely-structured bibliographic citation of which the sub-components may or may not be explicitly tagged. [3.12.1. Methods of Encoding Bibliographic References and Lists of References 2.2.7. The Source Description 16.3.2. Declarable Elements]

rng:element.name: biblStruct
rng:element.a:documentation: (structured bibliographic citation) contains a structured bibliographic citation, in which only bibliographic sub-elements appear and in a specified order. [3.12.1. Methods of Encoding Bibliographic References and Lists of References 2.2.7. The Source Description 16.3.2. Declarable Elements]

rng:element.name: listBibl
rng:element.a:documentation: (citation list) contains a list of bibliographic citations of any kind. [3.12.1. Methods of Encoding Bibliographic References and Lists of References 2.2.7. The Source Description 16.3.2. Declarable Elements]

rng:element.name: relatedItem
rng:element.a:documentation: contains or references some other bibliographic item which is related to the present one in some specified manner, for example as a constituent or alternative version of it. [3.12.2.7. Related Items]

sch:rule.sch:report: If the @target attribute on is used, the relatedItem element must be empty.
sch:rule.sch:assert: A relatedItem element should have either a @target attribute or a child element to indicate the related bibliographic item.

rng:attribute.name: target
rng:attribute.a:documentation: points to the related bibliographic element by means of an absolute or relative URI reference.

rng:element.name: l
rng:element.a:documentation: (verse line) contains a single, possibly incomplete, line of verse. [3.13.1. Core Tags for Verse 3.13. Passages of Verse or Drama 7.2.6. Speech Contents]

sch:rule.sch:report: Abstract model violation: Metrical lines (<l> elements) may not contain <l> or <lg> elements.

rng:element.name: lg
rng:element.a:documentation: (line group) contains one or more verse lines functioning as a formal unit, e.g. a stanza, refrain, verse paragraph, etc. [3.13.1. Core Tags for Verse 3.13. Passages of Verse or Drama 7.2.6. Speech Contents]

sch:rule.sch:assert: An <lg> element must contain at least one child <l>, <lg>, or <gap> element.

sch:rule.sch:report: Abstract model violation: Lines may not contain line groups.

rng:element.name: sp
rng:element.a:documentation: (speech) contains an individual speech in a performance text, or a passage presented as such in a prose or verse text. [3.13.2. Core Tags for Drama 3.13. Passages of Verse or Drama 7.2.2. Speeches and Speakers]

rng:element.name: speaker
rng:element.a:documentation: contains a specialized form of heading or label, giving the name of one or more speakers in a dramatic text or fragment. [3.13.2. Core Tags for Drama]

rng:element.name: stage
rng:element.a:documentation: (stage direction) contains any kind of stage direction within a dramatic text or fragment. [3.13.2. Core Tags for Drama 3.13. Passages of Verse or Drama 7.2.5. Stage Directions]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates the kind of stage direction. Suggested values include: 1] setting; 2] entrance; 3] exit; 4] business; 5] novelistic; 6] delivery; 7] modifier; 8] location; 9] mixed

rng:choice.a:documentation: describes a setting.
describes an entrance.
describes an exit.
describes stage business.
is a narrative, motivating stage direction.
describes how a character speaks.
gives some detail about a character.
describes a location.
more than one of the above

rng:element.name: teiCorpus
rng:element.a:documentation: (TEI corpus) contains the whole of a TEI encoded corpus, comprising a single corpus header and one or more <TEI> elements, each containing a single text header and a text. [4. Default Text Structure 16.1. Varieties of Composite Text]

rng:attribute.name: version
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (version) specifies the version number of the TEI Guidelines against which this document is valid.

rng:element.name: divGen
rng:element.a:documentation: (automatically generated text division) indicates the location at which a textual division generated automatically by a text-processing application is to appear. [3.9.2. Index Entries]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies what type of generated text division (e.g. index, table of contents, etc.) is to appear. Sample values include: 1] index; 2] toc; 3] figlist; 4] tablist

rng:element.name: textLang
rng:element.a:documentation: (text language) describes the languages and writing systems identified within the bibliographic work being described, rather than its description. [3.12.2.4. Imprint, Size of a Document, and Reprint Information 11.6.6. Languages and Writing Systems]

rng:attribute.name: mainLang
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (main language) supplies a code which identifies the chief language used in the bibliographic work.

rng:attribute.name: otherLangs
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (other languages) one or more codes identifying any other languages used in the bibliographic work.

rng:attribute.name: use
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (use) supplies an XPath selection pattern using the syntax defined in . The XPath pattern is relative to the context given in @match, which will either be a sibling attribute in the case of `<citeStructure>` or on the parent `<citeStructure>` in the case of `<citeData>`.

rng:attribute.name: matchPattern
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies a regular expression against which the values of other attributes can be matched.

rng:attribute.name: replacementPattern
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies a replacement pattern, that is, the skeleton of a relative or absolute URI containing references to groups in the @matchPattern which, once subpattern substitution has been performed, complete the URI.

rng:element.name: teiHeader
rng:element.a:documentation: (TEI header) supplies descriptive and declarative metadata associated with a digital resource or set of resources. [2.1.1. The TEI Header and Its Components 16.1. Varieties of Composite Text]

rng:element.name: fileDesc
rng:element.a:documentation: (file description) contains a full bibliographic description of an electronic file. [2.2. The File Description 2.1.1. The TEI Header and Its Components]

rng:element.name: titleStmt
rng:element.a:documentation: (title statement) groups information about the title of a work and those responsible for its content. [2.2.1. The Title Statement 2.2. The File Description]

rng:element.name: sponsor
rng:element.a:documentation: (sponsor) specifies the name of a sponsoring organization or institution. [2.2.1. The Title Statement]

rng:element.name: funder
rng:element.a:documentation: (funding body) specifies the name of an individual, institution, or organization responsible for the funding of a project or text. [2.2.1. The Title Statement]

rng:element.name: principal
rng:element.a:documentation: (principal researcher) supplies the name of the principal researcher responsible for the creation of an electronic text. [2.2.1. The Title Statement]

rng:element.name: editionStmt
rng:element.a:documentation: (edition statement) groups information relating to one edition of a text. [2.2.2. The Edition Statement 2.2. The File Description]

rng:element.name: edition
rng:element.a:documentation: (edition) describes the particularities of one edition of a text. [2.2.2. The Edition Statement]

rng:element.name: extent
rng:element.a:documentation: (extent) describes the approximate size of a text stored on some carrier medium or of some other object, digital or non-digital, specified in any convenient units. [2.2.3. Type and Extent of File 2.2. The File Description 3.12.2.4. Imprint, Size of a Document, and Reprint Information 11.7.1. Object Description]

rng:element.name: publicationStmt
rng:element.a:documentation: (publication statement) groups information concerning the publication or distribution of an electronic or other text. [2.2.4. Publication, Distribution, Licensing, etc. 2.2. The File Description]

rng:element.name: distributor
rng:element.a:documentation: (distributor) supplies the name of a person or other agency responsible for the distribution of a text. [2.2.4. Publication, Distribution, Licensing, etc.]

rng:element.name: authority
rng:element.a:documentation: (release authority) supplies the name of a person or other agency responsible for making a work available, other than a publisher or distributor. [2.2.4. Publication, Distribution, Licensing, etc.]

rng:element.name: idno
rng:element.a:documentation: (identifier) supplies any form of identifier used to identify some object, such as a bibliographic item, a person, a title, an organization, etc. in a standardized way. [14.3.1. Basic Principles 2.2.4. Publication, Distribution, Licensing, etc. 2.2.5. The Series Statement 3.12.2.4. Imprint, Size of a Document, and Reprint Information]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: categorizes the identifier, for example as an ISBN, Social Security number, etc. Suggested values include: 1] ISBN; 2] ISSN; 3] DOI; 4] URI; 5] VIAF; 6] ESTC; 7] OCLC

rng:choice.a:documentation: International Standard Book Number: a 13- or (if assigned prior to 2007) 10-digit identifying number assigned by the publishing industry to a published book or similar item, registered with the International ISBN Agency.
International Standard Serial Number: an eight-digit number to uniquely identify a serial publication.
Digital Object Identifier: a unique string of letters and numbers assigned to an electronic document.
Uniform Resource Identifier: a string of characters to uniquely identify a resource, following the syntax of RFC 3986.
A data number in the Virtual Internet Authority File assigned to link different names in catalogs around the world for the same entity.
English Short-Title Catalogue number: an identifying number assigned to a document in English printed in the British Isles or North America before 1801.
OCLC control number (record number) for the union catalog record in WorldCat, a union catalog for member libraries in the Online Computer Library Center global cooperative.

rng:element.name: availability
rng:element.a:documentation: (availability) supplies information about the availability of a text, for example any restrictions on its use or distribution, its copyright status, any licence applying to it, etc. [2.2.4. Publication, Distribution, Licensing, etc.]

rng:attribute.name: status
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (status) supplies a code identifying the current availability of the text.

rng:choice.a:documentation: (free) the text is freely available.
(unknown) the status of the text is unknown.
(restricted) the text is not freely available.

rng:element.name: licence
rng:element.a:documentation: contains information about a licence or other legal agreement applicable to the text. [2.2.4. Publication, Distribution, Licensing, etc.]

rng:element.name: seriesStmt
rng:element.a:documentation: (series statement) groups information about the series, if any, to which a publication belongs. [2.2.5. The Series Statement 2.2. The File Description]

rng:element.name: notesStmt
rng:element.a:documentation: (notes statement) collects together any notes providing information about a text additional to that recorded in other parts of the bibliographic description. [2.2.6. The Notes Statement 2.2. The File Description]

rng:element.name: sourceDesc
rng:element.a:documentation: (source description) describes the source(s) from which an electronic text was derived or generated, typically a bibliographic description in the case of a digitized text, or a phrase such as born digital for a text which has no previous existence. [2.2.7. The Source Description]

rng:element.name: biblFull
rng:element.a:documentation: (fully-structured bibliographic citation) contains a fully-structured bibliographic citation, in which all components of the TEI file description are present. [3.12.1. Methods of Encoding Bibliographic References and Lists of References 2.2. The File Description 2.2.7. The Source Description 16.3.2. Declarable Elements]

rng:element.name: encodingDesc
rng:element.a:documentation: (encoding description) documents the relationship between an electronic text and the source or sources from which it was derived. [2.3. The Encoding Description 2.1.1. The TEI Header and Its Components]

rng:element.name: schemaRef
rng:element.a:documentation: (schema reference) describes or points to a related customization or schema file. [2.3.10. The Schema Specification]

rng:attribute.name: key
rng:attribute.a:documentation: the identifier used for the customization or schema.

rng:element.name: projectDesc
rng:element.a:documentation: (project description) describes in detail the aim or purpose for which an electronic file was encoded, together with any other relevant information concerning the process by which it was assembled or collected. [2.3.1. The Project Description 2.3. The Encoding Description 16.3.2. Declarable Elements]

rng:element.name: samplingDecl
rng:element.a:documentation: (sampling declaration) contains a prose description of the rationale and methods used in selecting texts, or parts of a text, for inclusion in the resource. [2.3.2. The Sampling Declaration 2.3. The Encoding Description 16.3.2. Declarable Elements]

rng:element.name: editorialDecl
rng:element.a:documentation: (editorial practice declaration) provides details of editorial principles and practices applied during the encoding of a text. [2.3.3. The Editorial Practices Declaration 2.3. The Encoding Description 16.3.2. Declarable Elements]

rng:element.name: correction
rng:element.a:documentation: (correction principles) states how and under what circumstances corrections have been made in the text. [2.3.3. The Editorial Practices Declaration 16.3.2. Declarable Elements]

rng:attribute.name: status
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates the degree of correction applied to the text.

rng:choice.a:documentation: the text has been thoroughly checked and proofread.
the text has been checked at least once.
the text has not been checked.
the correction status of the text is unknown.

rng:attribute.name: method
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates the method adopted to indicate corrections within the text.

rng:choice.a:documentation: corrections have been made silently
corrections have been represented using markup

rng:element.name: normalization
rng:element.a:documentation: (normalization) indicates the extent of normalization or regularization of the original source carried out in converting it to electronic form. [2.3.3. The Editorial Practices Declaration 16.3.2. Declarable Elements]

rng:attribute.name: method
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates the method adopted to indicate normalizations within the text.

rng:choice.a:documentation: normalization made silently
normalization represented using markup

rng:element.name: quotation
rng:element.a:documentation: (quotation) specifies editorial practice adopted with respect to quotation marks in the original. [2.3.3. The Editorial Practices Declaration 16.3.2. Declarable Elements]

sch:rule.sch:report: On <>, either the @marks attribute should be used, or a paragraph of description provided.

rng:attribute.name: marks
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (quotation marks) indicates whether or not quotation marks have been retained as content within the text.

rng:choice.a:documentation: no quotation marks have been retained
some quotation marks have been retained
all quotation marks have been retained

rng:element.name: hyphenation
rng:element.a:documentation: (hyphenation) summarizes the way in which hyphenation in a source text has been treated in an encoded version of it. [2.3.3. The Editorial Practices Declaration 16.3.2. Declarable Elements]

rng:attribute.name: eol
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (end-of-line) indicates whether or not end-of-line hyphenation has been retained in a text.

rng:choice.a:documentation: all end-of-line hyphenation has been retained, even though the lineation of the original may not have been.
end-of-line hyphenation has been retained in some cases.
all soft end-of-line hyphenation has been removed: any remaining end-of-line hyphenation should be retained.
all end-of-line hyphenation has been removed: any remaining hyphenation occurred within the line.

rng:element.name: segmentation
rng:element.a:documentation: (segmentation) describes the principles according to which the text has been segmented, for example into sentences, tone-units, graphemic strata, etc. [2.3.3. The Editorial Practices Declaration 16.3.2. Declarable Elements]

rng:element.name: stdVals
rng:element.a:documentation: (standard values) specifies the format used when standardized date or number values are supplied. [2.3.3. The Editorial Practices Declaration 16.3.2. Declarable Elements]

rng:element.name: interpretation
rng:element.a:documentation: (interpretation) describes the scope of any analytic or interpretive information added to the text in addition to the transcription. [2.3.3. The Editorial Practices Declaration]

rng:element.name: punctuation
rng:element.a:documentation: specifies editorial practice adopted with respect to punctuation marks in the original. [2.3.3. The Editorial Practices Declaration 3.2. Treatment of Punctuation]

rng:attribute.name: marks
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates whether or not punctation marks have been retained as content within the text.

rng:choice.a:documentation: no punctuation marks have been retained
some punctuation marks have been retained
all punctuation marks have been retained

rng:attribute.name: placement
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates the positioning of punctuation marks that are associated with marked up text as being encoded within the element surrounding the text or immediately before or after it.

rng:choice.a:documentation: punctuation marks found at the start or end of a marked up text component are included within its surrounding element;
punctuation marks found at the start or end of a marked up text component appear immediately before or after the surrounding element

rng:element.name: tagsDecl
rng:element.a:documentation: (tagging declaration) provides detailed information about the tagging applied to a document. [2.3.4. The Tagging Declaration 2.3. The Encoding Description]

rng:attribute.name: partial
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates whether the element types listed exhaustively include all those found within <text>, or represent only a subset.

rng:element.name: tagUsage
rng:element.a:documentation: (element usage) documents the usage of a specific element within a specified document. [2.3.4. The Tagging Declaration]

rng:attribute.name: gi
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (generic identifier) specifies the name (generic identifier) of the element indicated by the tag, within the namespace indicated by the parent <namespace> element.

rng:attribute.name: occurs
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the number of occurrences of this element within the text.

rng:attribute.name: withId
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (with unique identifier) specifies the number of occurrences of this element within the text which bear a distinct value for the global @xml:id attribute.

rng:element.name: namespace
rng:element.a:documentation: (namespace) supplies the formal name of the namespace to which the elements documented by its children belong. [2.3.4. The Tagging Declaration]

rng:attribute.name: name
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the full formal name of the namespace concerned.

rng:element.name: rendition
rng:element.a:documentation: (rendition) supplies information about the rendition or appearance of one or more elements in the source text. [2.3.4. The Tagging Declaration]

rng:attribute.name: scope
rng:attribute.a:documentation: where CSS is used, provides a way of defining pseudo-elements, that is, styling rules applicable to specific sub-portions of an element. Sample values include: 1] first-line; 2] first-letter; 3] before; 4] after

rng:attribute.name: selector
rng:attribute.a:documentation: contains a selector or series of selectors specifying the elements to which the contained style description applies, expressed in the language specified in the @scheme attribute.

rng:element.name: styleDefDecl
rng:element.a:documentation: (style definition language declaration) specifies the name of the formal language in which style or renditional information is supplied elsewhere in the document. The specific version of the scheme may also be supplied. [2.3.5. The Default Style Definition Language Declaration]

rng:element.name: refsDecl
rng:element.a:documentation: (references declaration) specifies how canonical references are constructed for this text. [2.3.6.3. Milestone Method 2.3. The Encoding Description 2.3.6. The Reference System Declaration]

rng:element.name: citeStructure
rng:element.a:documentation: (citation structure) declares a structure and method for citing the current document. [3.11.4. Declaring Reference Systems 17.2.5.4. Citation Structures]

rng:attribute.name: delim
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (delimiter) supplies a delimiting string preceding the structural component.

rng:attribute.name: match
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (match) supplies an XPath selection pattern using the syntax defined in which identifies a set of nodes which are citable structural components. The expression may be absolute (beginning with `/`) or relative. @match on a <citeStructure> without a <citeStructure> parent must be an absolute XPath. If it is relative, its context is set by the @match of the parent <citeStructure>.

sch:rule.sch:assert: An XPath in @match on the outer <> must start with '/'.
An XPath in @match must not start with '/' except on the outer <>.

rng:attribute.name: unit
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (unit) describes the structural unit indicated by the <citeStructure>. Sample values include: 1] book; 2] chapter; 3] entry; 4] poem; 5] letter; 6] line; 7] section; 8] verse; 9] volume

rng:element.name: citeData
rng:element.a:documentation: (citation data) specifies how information may be extracted from citation structures. [3.11.4. Declaring Reference Systems 17.2.5.4. Citation Structures]

rng:attribute.name: property
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (property) A URI indicating a property definition.

rng:element.name: cRefPattern
rng:element.a:documentation: (canonical reference pattern) specifies an expression and replacement pattern for transforming a canonical reference into a URI. [2.3.6.3. Milestone Method 2.3.6. The Reference System Declaration 2.3.6.2. Search-and-Replace Method]

rng:element.name: prefixDef
rng:element.a:documentation: (prefix definition) defines a prefixing scheme used in teidata.pointer values, showing how abbreviated URIs using the scheme may be expanded into full URIs. [17.2.3. Using Abbreviated Pointers]

rng:attribute.name: ident
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies a name which functions as the prefix for an abbreviated pointing scheme such as a private URI scheme. The prefix constitutes the text preceding the first colon.

rng:element.name: listPrefixDef
rng:element.a:documentation: (list of prefix definitions) contains a list of definitions of prefixing schemes used in teidata.pointer values, showing how abbreviated URIs using each scheme may be expanded into full URIs. [17.2.3. Using Abbreviated Pointers]

rng:element.name: refState
rng:element.a:documentation: (reference state) specifies one component of a canonical reference defined by the milestone method. [2.3.6.3. Milestone Method 2.3.6. The Reference System Declaration]

rng:attribute.name: length
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the fixed length of the reference component.

rng:attribute.name: delim
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (delimiter) supplies a delimiting string following the reference component.

rng:element.name: classDecl
rng:element.a:documentation: (classification declarations) contains one or more taxonomies defining any classificatory codes used elsewhere in the text. [2.3.7. The Classification Declaration 2.3. The Encoding Description]

rng:element.name: taxonomy
rng:element.a:documentation: (taxonomy) defines a typology either implicitly, by means of a bibliographic citation, or explicitly by a structured taxonomy. [2.3.7. The Classification Declaration]

rng:element.name: category
rng:element.a:documentation: (category) contains an individual descriptive category, possibly nested within a superordinate category, within a user-defined taxonomy. [2.3.7. The Classification Declaration]

rng:element.name: catDesc
rng:element.a:documentation: (category description) describes some category within a taxonomy or text typology, either in the form of a brief prose description or in terms of the situational parameters used by the TEI formal <textDesc>. [2.3.7. The Classification Declaration]

rng:element.name: geoDecl
rng:element.a:documentation: (geographic coordinates declaration) documents the notation and the datum used for geographic coordinates expressed as content of the <geo> element elsewhere within the document. [2.3.8. The Geographic Coordinates Declaration]

rng:attribute.name: datum
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies a commonly used code name for the datum employed. Suggested values include: 1] WGS84 (World Geodetic System); 2] MGRS (Military Grid Reference System); 3] OSGB36 (ordnance survey great britain); 4] ED50 (European Datum coordinate system)

rng:choice.a:documentation: (World Geodetic System) a pair of numbers to be interpreted as latitude followed by longitude according to the World Geodetic System.

(Military Grid Reference System) values supplied follow the Military Grid Reference System, which designates grid zones in a string of letters and numbers that distinctly indicate each square meter on the planet.
(ordnance survey great britain) the value supplied is to be interpreted as a British National Grid Reference.
(European Datum coordinate system) the value supplied is to be interpreted as latitude followed by longitude according to the European Datum coordinate system.

rng:element.name: unitDecl
rng:element.a:documentation: (unit declarations) provides information about units of measurement that are not members of the International System of Units. [2.3.9. The Unit Declaration]

rng:element.name: unitDef
rng:element.a:documentation: (unit definition) contains descriptive information related to a specific unit of measurement. [2.3.9. The Unit Declaration]

rng:element.name: conversion
rng:element.a:documentation: defines how to calculate one unit of measure in terms of another. [2.3.9. The Unit Declaration]

rng:attribute.name: fromUnit
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates a source unit of measure that is to be converted into another unit indicated in @toUnit.

rng:attribute.name: toUnit
rng:attribute.a:documentation: the target unit of measurement for a conversion from a source unit referenced in @fromUnit.

rng:element.name: appInfo
rng:element.a:documentation: (application information) records information about an application which has edited the TEI file. [2.3.11. The Application Information Element]

rng:element.name: application
rng:element.a:documentation: provides information about an application which has acted upon the document. [2.3.11. The Application Information Element]

rng:attribute.name: ident
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies an identifier for the application, independent of its version number or display name.

rng:attribute.name: version
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies a version number for the application, independent of its identifier or display name.

rng:element.name: profileDesc
rng:element.a:documentation: (text-profile description) provides a detailed description of non-bibliographic aspects of a text, specifically the languages and sublanguages used, the situation in which it was produced, the participants and their setting. [2.4. The Profile Description 2.1.1. The TEI Header and Its Components]

rng:element.name: handNote
rng:element.a:documentation: (note on hand) describes a particular style or hand distinguished within a manuscript. [11.7.2. Writing, Decoration, and Other Notations]

rng:element.name: abstract
rng:element.a:documentation: contains a summary or formal abstract prefixed to an existing source document by the encoder. [2.4.4. Abstracts]

rng:element.name: creation
rng:element.a:documentation: (creation) contains information about the creation of a text. [2.4.1. Creation 2.4. The Profile Description]

rng:element.name: langUsage
rng:element.a:documentation: (language usage) describes the languages, sublanguages, registers, dialects, etc. represented within a text. [2.4.2. Language Usage 2.4. The Profile Description 16.3.2. Declarable Elements]

rng:element.name: language
rng:element.a:documentation: (language) characterizes a single language or sublanguage used within a text. [2.4.2. Language Usage]

rng:attribute.name: ident
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (identifier) Supplies a language code constructed as defined in BCP 47 which is used to identify the language documented by this element, and which may be referenced by the global @xml:lang attribute.

rng:attribute.name: usage
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the approximate percentage of the text which uses this language.

rng:element.name: textClass
rng:element.a:documentation: (text classification) groups information which describes the nature or topic of a text in terms of a standard classification scheme, thesaurus, etc. [2.4.3. The Text Classification]

rng:element.name: keywords
rng:element.a:documentation: (keywords) contains a list of keywords or phrases identifying the topic or nature of a text. [2.4.3. The Text Classification]

rng:attribute.name: scheme
rng:attribute.a:documentation: identifies the controlled vocabulary within which the set of keywords concerned is defined, for example by a <taxonomy> element, or by some other resource.

rng:element.name: classCode
rng:element.a:documentation: (classification code) contains the classification code used for this text in some standard classification system. [2.4.3. The Text Classification]

rng:attribute.name: scheme
rng:attribute.a:documentation: identifies the classification system in use, as defined by, e.g. a <taxonomy> element, or some other resource.

rng:element.name: catRef
rng:element.a:documentation: (category reference) specifies one or more defined categories within some taxonomy or text typology. [2.4.3. The Text Classification]

rng:attribute.name: scheme
rng:attribute.a:documentation: identifies the classification scheme within which the set of categories concerned is defined, for example by a <taxonomy> element, or by some other resource.

rng:element.name: calendarDesc
rng:element.a:documentation: (calendar description) contains a description of the calendar system used in any dating expression found in the text. [2.4. The Profile Description 2.4.5. Calendar Description]

rng:element.name: calendar
rng:element.a:documentation: (calendar) describes a calendar or dating system used in a dating formula in the text. [2.4.5. Calendar Description]

rng:element.name: correspDesc
rng:element.a:documentation: (correspondence description) contains a description of the actions related to one act of correspondence. [2.4.6. Correspondence Description]

rng:element.name: correspAction
rng:element.a:documentation: (correspondence action) contains a structured description of the place, the name of a person/organization and the date related to the sending/receiving of a message or any other action related to the correspondence. [2.4.6. Correspondence Description]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: describes the nature of the action. Suggested values include: 1] sent; 2] received; 3] transmitted; 4] redirected; 5] forwarded

rng:choice.a:documentation: information concerning the sending or dispatch of a message.
information concerning the receipt of a message.
information concerning the transmission of a message, i.e. between the dispatch and the next receipt, redirect or forwarding.
information concerning the redirection of an unread message.
information concerning the forwarding of a message.

rng:element.name: correspContext
rng:element.a:documentation: (correspondence context) provides references to preceding or following correspondence related to this piece of correspondence. [2.4.6. Correspondence Description]

rng:element.name: xenoData
rng:element.a:documentation: (non-TEI metadata) provides a container element into which metadata in non-TEI formats may be placed. [2.5. Non-TEI Metadata]

rng:element.name: revisionDesc
rng:element.a:documentation: (revision description) summarizes the revision history for a file. [2.6. The Revision Description 2.1.1. The TEI Header and Its Components]

rng:element.name: change
rng:element.a:documentation: (change) documents a change or set of changes made during the production of a source document, or during the revision of an electronic file. [2.6. The Revision Description 2.4.1. Creation 12.7. Identifying Changes and Revisions]

rng:attribute.name: target
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (target) points to one or more elements that belong to this change.

rng:element.name: scriptNote
rng:element.a:documentation: describes a particular script distinguished within the description of a manuscript or similar resource. [11.7.2. Writing, Decoration, and Other Notations]

rng:element.name: listChange
rng:element.a:documentation: groups a number of change descriptions associated with either the creation of a source text or the revision of an encoded text. [2.6. The Revision Description 12.7. Identifying Changes and Revisions]

rng:attribute.name: ordered
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates whether the ordering of its child <change> elements is to be considered significant or not.

rng:element.name: TEI
rng:element.a:documentation: (TEI document) contains a single TEI-conformant document, combining a single TEI header with one or more members of the model.resource class. Multiple <TEI> elements may be combined within a <TEI> (or <teiCorpus>) element. [4. Default Text Structure 16.1. Varieties of Composite Text]

rng:attribute.name: version
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the version number of the TEI Guidelines against which this document is valid.

rng:element.name: text
rng:element.a:documentation: (text) contains a single text of any kind, whether unitary or composite, for example a poem or drama, a collection of essays, a novel, a dictionary, or a corpus sample. [4. Default Text Structure 16.1. Varieties of Composite Text]

rng:element.name: body
rng:element.a:documentation: (text body) contains the whole body of a single unitary text, excluding any front or back matter. [4. Default Text Structure]

rng:element.name: group
rng:element.a:documentation: (group) contains the body of a composite text, grouping together a sequence of distinct texts (or groups of such texts) which are regarded as a unit for some purpose, for example the collected works of an author, a sequence of prose essays, etc. [4. Default Text Structure 4.3.1. Grouped Texts 16.1. Varieties of Composite Text]

rng:element.name: floatingText
rng:element.a:documentation: (floating text) contains a single text of any kind, whether unitary or composite, which interrupts the text containing it at any point and after which the surrounding text resumes. [4.3.2. Floating Texts]

rng:element.name: div
rng:element.a:documentation: (text division) contains a subdivision of the front, body, or back of a text. [4.1. Divisions of the Body]

sch:rule.sch:assert: Abstract model violation: Metrical lines (<l> elements) may not contain higher-level structural elements such as <div>, unless <div> is a descendant of <floatingText>.

rng:element.name: div1
rng:element.a:documentation: (level-1 text division) contains a first-level subdivision of the front, body, or back of a text. [4.1.2. Numbered Divisions]

rng:element.name: div2
rng:element.a:documentation: (level-2 text division) contains a second-level subdivision of the front, body, or back of a text. [4.1.2. Numbered Divisions]

rng:element.name: div3
rng:element.a:documentation: (level-3 text division) contains a third-level subdivision of the front, body, or back of a text. [4.1.2. Numbered Divisions]

rng:element.name: div4
rng:element.a:documentation: (level-4 text division) contains a fourth-level subdivision of the front, body, or back of a text. [4.1.2. Numbered Divisions]

rng:element.name: div5
rng:element.a:documentation: (level-5 text division) contains a fifth-level subdivision of the front, body, or back of a text. [4.1.2. Numbered Divisions]

rng:element.name: div6
rng:element.a:documentation: (level-6 text division) contains a sixth-level subdivision of the front, body, or back of a text. [4.1.2. Numbered Divisions]

rng:element.name: div7
rng:element.a:documentation: (level-7 text division) contains the smallest possible subdivision of the front, body or back of a text, larger than a paragraph. [4.1.2. Numbered Divisions]

rng:element.name: trailer
rng:element.a:documentation: contains a closing title or footer appearing at the end of a division of a text. [4.2.4. Content of Textual Divisions 4.2. Elements Common to All Divisions]

rng:element.name: byline
rng:element.a:documentation: (byline) contains the primary statement of responsibility given for a work on its title page or at the head or end of the work. [4.2.2. Openers and Closers 4.5. Front Matter]

rng:element.name: dateline
rng:element.a:documentation: (dateline) contains a brief description of the place, date, time, etc. of production of a letter, newspaper story, or other work, prefixed or suffixed to it as a kind of heading or trailer. [4.2.2. Openers and Closers]

rng:element.name: argument
rng:element.a:documentation: (argument) contains a formal list or prose description of the topics addressed by a subdivision of a text. [4.2. Elements Common to All Divisions 4.6. Title Pages]

rng:element.name: epigraph
rng:element.a:documentation: (epigraph) contains a quotation, anonymous or attributed, appearing at the start or end of a section or on a title page. [4.2.3. Arguments, Epigraphs, and Postscripts 4.2. Elements Common to All Divisions 4.6. Title Pages]

rng:element.name: opener
rng:element.a:documentation: (opener) groups together dateline, byline, salutation, and similar phrases appearing as a preliminary group at the start of a division, especially of a letter. [4.2. Elements Common to All Divisions]

rng:element.name: closer
rng:element.a:documentation: (closer) groups together salutations, datelines, bylines, and similar phrases appearing as a final group at the end of a division, especially of a letter. [4.2.2. Openers and Closers 4.2. Elements Common to All Divisions]

rng:element.name: salute
rng:element.a:documentation: (salutation) contains a salutation or greeting prefixed to a foreword, dedicatory epistle, or other division of a text, or the salutation in the closing of a letter, preface, etc. [4.2.2. Openers and Closers]

rng:element.name: signed
rng:element.a:documentation: (signature) contains the closing salutation, etc., appended to a foreword, dedicatory epistle, or other division of a text. [4.2.2. Openers and Closers]

rng:element.name: postscript
rng:element.a:documentation: contains a postscript, e.g. to a letter. [4.2. Elements Common to All Divisions]

rng:element.name: titlePage
rng:element.a:documentation: (title page) contains the title page of a text, appearing within the front or back matter. [4.6. Title Pages]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: classifies the title page according to any convenient typology.

rng:element.name: docTitle
rng:element.a:documentation: (document title) contains the title of a document, including all its constituents, as given on a title page. [4.6. Title Pages]

rng:element.name: titlePart
rng:element.a:documentation: (title part) contains a subsection or division of the title of a work, as indicated on a title page. [4.6. Title Pages]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (type) specifies the role of this subdivision of the title. Suggested values include: 1] main (main); 2] sub (subordinate); 3] alt (alternate); 4] short (short); 5] desc (descriptive)

rng:choice.a:documentation: (main) main title of the work
(subordinate) subtitle of the work
(alternate) alternative title of the work
(short) abbreviated form of title
(descriptive) descriptive paraphrase of the work

rng:element.name: docAuthor
rng:element.a:documentation: (document author) contains the name of the author of the document, as given on the title page (often but not always contained in a byline). [4.6. Title Pages]

rng:element.name: imprimatur
rng:element.a:documentation: (imprimatur) contains a formal statement authorizing the publication of a work, sometimes required to appear on a title page or its verso. [4.6. Title Pages]

rng:element.name: docEdition
rng:element.a:documentation: (document edition) contains an edition statement as presented on a title page of a document. [4.6. Title Pages]

rng:element.name: docImprint
rng:element.a:documentation: (document imprint) contains the imprint statement (place and date of publication, publisher name), as given (usually) at the foot of a title page. [4.6. Title Pages]

rng:element.name: docDate
rng:element.a:documentation: (document date) contains the date of a document, as given on a title page or in a dateline. [4.6. Title Pages]

rng:element.name: front
rng:element.a:documentation: (front matter) contains any prefatory matter (headers, abstracts, title page, prefaces, dedications, etc.) found at the start of a document, before the main body. [4.6. Title Pages 4. Default Text Structure]

rng:element.name: back
rng:element.a:documentation: (back matter) contains any appendixes, etc. following the main part of a text. [4.7. Back Matter 4. Default Text Structure]

rng:attribute.name: name
rng:attribute.a:documentation: provides the name of the character or glyph property being defined.

rng:attribute.name: value
rng:attribute.a:documentation: provides the value of the character or glyph property being defined.

rng:attribute.name: scheme
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies the name of the character set system from which this property is drawn. Sample values include: 1] Unicode (Unicode); 2] Bridwell (E. Nelson Bridwell); 3] Brewer (Georg Brewer); 4] Doyle (Darren Doyle); 5] Schreyer (Christine Schreyer)

rng:element.name: g
rng:element.a:documentation: (character or glyph) represents a glyph, or a non-standard character. [5. Characters, Glyphs, and Writing Modes]

rng:attribute.name: ref
rng:attribute.a:documentation: points to a description of the character or glyph intended.

rng:element.name: charDecl
rng:element.a:documentation: (character declarations) provides information about nonstandard characters and glyphs. [5.2. Markup Constructs for Representation of Characters and Glyphs]

rng:element.name: char
rng:element.a:documentation: (character) provides descriptive information about a character. [5.2. Markup Constructs for Representation of Characters and Glyphs]

rng:element.name: glyph
rng:element.a:documentation: (character glyph) provides descriptive information about a character glyph. [5.2. Markup Constructs for Representation of Characters and Glyphs]

rng:element.name: localProp
rng:element.a:documentation: (locally defined property) provides a locally defined character (or glyph) property. [5.2.1. Character Properties]

rng:element.name: mapping
rng:element.a:documentation: (character mapping) contains one or more characters which are related to the parent character or glyph in some respect, as specified by the @type attribute. [5.2. Markup Constructs for Representation of Characters and Glyphs]

rng:element.name: unihanProp
rng:element.a:documentation: (unihan property) holds the name and value of a normative or informative Unihan character (or glyph) property as part of its attributes. [5.2.1. Character Properties]

rng:attribute.name: name
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the normalized name of a unicode han database (Unihan) property.

rng:attribute.name: value
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the value of a named Unihan property

rng:element.name: unicodeProp
rng:element.a:documentation: (unicode property) provides a Unicode property for a character (or glyph). [5.2.1. Character Properties]

rng:attribute.name: name
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the normalized name of a Unicode property.

rng:attribute.name: value
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the value of a named Unicode property.

rng:attribute.name: met
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (metrical structure, conventional) contains a user-specified encoding for the conventional metrical structure of the element.

rng:attribute.name: real
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (metrical structure, realized) contains a user-specified encoding for the actual realization of the conventional metrical structure applicable to the element.

rng:attribute.name: rhyme
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (rhyme scheme) specifies the rhyme scheme applicable to a group of verse lines.

rng:attribute.name: enjamb
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (enjambement) indicates that the end of a verse line is marked by enjambement. Sample values include: 1] no; 2] yes; 3] weak; 4] strong

rng:element.name: metDecl
rng:element.a:documentation: (metrical notation declaration) documents the notation employed to represent a metrical pattern when this is specified as the value of a @met, @real, or @rhyme attribute on any structural element of a metrical text (e.g. <lg>, <l>, or <seg>). [6.6. Metrical Notation Declaration 6.4. Rhyme and Metrical Analysis]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates whether the notation conveys the abstract metrical form, its actual prosodic realization, or the rhyme scheme, or some combination thereof.

rng:choice.a:documentation: (met attribute) declaration applies to the abstract metrical form recorded on the @met attribute
(real attribute) declaration applies to the actual realization of the conventional metrical structure recorded on the @real attribute
declaration applies to the rhyme scheme recorded on the @rhyme attribute
(met attribute) declaration applies to the abstract metrical form recorded on the @met attribute
(real attribute) declaration applies to the actual realization of the conventional metrical structure recorded on the @real attribute
declaration applies to the rhyme scheme recorded on the @rhyme attribute
(met attribute) declaration applies to the abstract metrical form recorded on the @met attribute
(real attribute) declaration applies to the actual realization of the conventional metrical structure recorded on the @real attribute
declaration applies to the rhyme scheme recorded on the @rhyme attribute

rng:attribute.name: pattern
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (regular expression pattern) specifies a regular expression defining any value that is legal for this notation.

rng:element.name: metSym
rng:element.a:documentation: (metrical notation symbol) documents the intended significance of a particular character or character sequence within a metrical notation, either explicitly or in terms of other <metSym> elements in the same <metDecl>. [6.6. Metrical Notation Declaration]

rng:attribute.name: value
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the character or character sequence being documented.

rng:attribute.name: terminal
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies whether the symbol is defined in terms of other symbols (@terminal is set to false) or in prose (@terminal is set to true).

rng:element.name: caesura
rng:element.a:documentation: marks the point at which a metrical line may be divided. [6.2. Components of the Verse Line]

rng:element.name: rhyme
rng:element.a:documentation: marks the rhyming part of a metrical line. [6.5. Rhyme]

rng:attribute.name: label
rng:attribute.a:documentation: provides a label (usually a single letter) to identify which part of a rhyme scheme this rhyming string instantiates.

rng:attribute.name: perf
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (performance) identifies the performance or performances in which this element occurred.

rng:element.name: set
rng:element.a:documentation: (setting) contains a description of the setting, time, locale, appearance, etc., of the action of a play, typically found in the front matter of a printed performance text (not a stage direction). [7.1. Front and Back Matter ]

rng:element.name: prologue
rng:element.a:documentation: (prologue) contains the prologue to a drama, typically spoken by an actor out of character, possibly in association with a particular performance or venue. [7.1.2. Prologues and Epilogues 7.1. Front and Back Matter ]

rng:element.name: epilogue
rng:element.a:documentation: (epilogue) contains the epilogue to a drama, typically spoken by an actor out of character, possibly in association with a particular performance or venue. [7.1.2. Prologues and Epilogues 7.1. Front and Back Matter ]

rng:element.name: performance
rng:element.a:documentation: (performance) contains a section of front or back matter describing how a dramatic piece is to be performed in general or how it was performed on some specific occasion. [7.1.3. Records of Performances 7.1. Front and Back Matter ]

rng:element.name: castList
rng:element.a:documentation: (cast list) contains a single cast list or dramatis personae. [7.1.4. Cast Lists 7.1. Front and Back Matter ]

rng:element.name: castGroup
rng:element.a:documentation: (cast list grouping) groups one or more individual <castItem> elements within a cast list. [7.1.4. Cast Lists]

rng:element.name: castItem
rng:element.a:documentation: (cast list item) contains a single entry within a cast list, describing either a single role or a list of non-speaking roles. [7.1.4. Cast Lists]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: characterizes the cast item.

rng:choice.a:documentation: the item describes a single role.
the item describes a list of non-speaking roles.

rng:element.name: role
rng:element.a:documentation: (role) contains the name of a dramatic role, as given in a cast list. [7.1.4. Cast Lists]

rng:attribute.name: gender
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the gender of the role.

rng:element.name: roleDesc
rng:element.a:documentation: (role description) describes a character's role in a drama. [7.1.4. Cast Lists]

rng:element.name: actor
rng:element.a:documentation: contains the name of an actor appearing within a cast list. [7.1.4. Cast Lists]

rng:attribute.name: sex
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the sex of the actor.

rng:attribute.name: gender
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the gender of the actor.

rng:element.name: spGrp
rng:element.a:documentation: (speech group) contains a group of speeches, speech groups, or songs in a performance text presented in a source as constituting a single unit or number. [7.2.3. Grouped Speeches]

rng:element.name: move
rng:element.a:documentation: (movement) marks the actual movement of one or more characters. [7.2.5. Stage Directions]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: characterizes the movement, for example as an entrance or exit. Suggested values include: 1] entrance; 2] exit; 3] onStage

rng:choice.a:documentation: character is entering the stage.
character is exiting the stage.
character moves on stage

rng:attribute.name: where
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the direction of a stage movement. Sample values include: 1] L (left); 2] R (right); 3] C (center)

rng:element.name: view
rng:element.a:documentation: (view) describes the visual context of some part of a screen play in terms of what the spectator sees, generally independent of any dialogue. [7.3.1. Technical Information 7.3. Other Types of Performance Text]

rng:element.name: camera
rng:element.a:documentation: (camera) describes a particular camera angle or viewpoint in a screen play. [7.3.1. Technical Information 7.3. Other Types of Performance Text]

rng:element.name: sound
rng:element.a:documentation: (sound) describes a sound effect or musical sequence specified within a screen play or radio script. [7.3.1. Technical Information 7.3. Other Types of Performance Text]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: categorizes the sound in some respect, e.g. as music, special effect, etc.

rng:attribute.name: discrete
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates whether the sound overlaps the surrounding speeches or interrupts them.

rng:element.name: caption
rng:element.a:documentation: (caption) contains the text of a caption or other text displayed as part of a film script or screenplay. [7.3.1. Technical Information 7.3. Other Types of Performance Text]

rng:element.name: tech
rng:element.a:documentation: (technical stage direction) describes a special-purpose stage direction that is not meant for the actors. [7.3.1. Technical Information]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: categorizes the technical stage direction. Suggested values include: 1] light; 2] sound; 3] prop; 4] block

rng:choice.a:documentation: a lighting cue
a sound cue
a prop cue
a blocking instruction

rng:element.name: scriptStmt
rng:element.a:documentation: (script statement) contains a citation giving details of the script used for a spoken text. [8.2. Documenting the Source of Transcribed Speech 2.2.7. The Source Description 16.3.2. Declarable Elements]

rng:element.name: recordingStmt
