rng:element.a:documentation: (recording statement) describes a set of recordings used as the basis for transcription of a spoken text. [8.2. Documenting the Source of Transcribed Speech 2.2.7. The Source Description]

rng:element.name: recording
rng:element.a:documentation: (recording event) provides details of an audio or video recording event used as the source of a spoken text, either directly or from a public broadcast. [8.2. Documenting the Source of Transcribed Speech 16.3.2. Declarable Elements]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: the kind of recording.

rng:choice.a:documentation: audio recording
audio and video recording

rng:element.name: equipment
rng:element.a:documentation: (equipment) provides technical details of the equipment and media used for an audio or video recording used as the source for a spoken text. [8.2. Documenting the Source of Transcribed Speech 16.3.2. Declarable Elements]

rng:element.name: broadcast
rng:element.a:documentation: (broadcast) describes a broadcast used as the source of a spoken text. [8.2. Documenting the Source of Transcribed Speech 16.3.2. Declarable Elements]

rng:element.name: transcriptionDesc
rng:element.a:documentation: (transcription description) describes the set of transcription conventions used, particularly for spoken material. [8.2. Documenting the Source of Transcribed Speech]

rng:attribute.name: ident
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies an identifier for the encoding convention, independent of any version number.

rng:attribute.name: version
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies a version number for the encoding conventions used, if any.

rng:element.name: u
rng:element.a:documentation: (utterance) contains a stretch of speech usually preceded and followed by silence or by a change of speaker. [8.3.1. Utterances]

rng:attribute.name: trans
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (transition) indicates the nature of the transition between this utterance and the previous one.

rng:choice.a:documentation: this utterance begins without unusual pause or rapidity.
this utterance begins with a markedly shorter pause than normal.
this utterance begins before the previous one has finished.
this utterance begins after a noticeable pause.

rng:element.name: pause
rng:element.a:documentation: (pause) marks a pause either between or within utterances. [8.3.2. Pausing]

rng:element.name: vocal
rng:element.a:documentation: (vocal) marks any vocalized but not necessarily lexical phenomenon, for example voiced pauses, non-lexical backchannels, etc. [8.3.3. Vocal, Kinesic, Incident]

rng:attribute.name: iterated
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates whether or not the phenomenon is repeated.

rng:element.name: kinesic
rng:element.a:documentation: (kinesic) marks any communicative phenomenon, not necessarily vocalized, for example a gesture, frown, etc. [8.3.3. Vocal, Kinesic, Incident]

rng:attribute.name: iterated
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates whether or not the phenomenon is repeated.

rng:element.name: incident
rng:element.a:documentation: (incident) marks any phenomenon or occurrence, not necessarily vocalized or communicative, for example incidental noises or other events affecting communication. [8.3.3. Vocal, Kinesic, Incident]

rng:element.name: writing
rng:element.a:documentation: (writing) contains a passage of written text revealed to participants in the course of a spoken text. [8.3.4. Writing]

rng:attribute.name: gradual
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates whether the writing is revealed all at once or gradually.

rng:element.name: shift
rng:element.a:documentation: (shift) marks the point at which some paralinguistic feature of a series of utterances by any one speaker changes. [8.3.6. Shifts]

sch:rule.sch:assert: The @new attribute should always be supplied; use the special value "normal" to indicate that the feature concerned ceases to be remarkable at this point.

rng:attribute.name: feature
rng:attribute.a:documentation: a paralinguistic feature. Suggested values include: 1] tempo; 2] loud; 3] pitch; 4] tension; 5] rhythm; 6] voice

rng:choice.a:documentation: speed of utterance.
loudness.
pitch range.
tension or stress pattern.
rhythmic qualities.
voice quality.

rng:attribute.name: new
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the new state of the paralinguistic feature specified.

rng:element.name: annotationBlock
rng:element.a:documentation: groups together various annotations, e.g. for parallel interpretations of a spoken segment. [8.4.6. Analytic Coding]

rng:element.name: post
rng:element.a:documentation: a written (or spoken) contribution to a CMC interaction which has been composed (or recorded) by its author in its entirety before being transmitted over a network (e.g., the internet) and made available on the monitor or screen of the other parties en bloc. [9.3.1. CMC Posts]

rng:attribute.name: modality
rng:attribute.a:documentation: written or spoken mode. Suggested values include: 1] written; 2] spoken (for audio (or audio-visual) posts)

rng:choice.a:documentation: for stretches of text and/or multimodal elements
(for audio (or audio-visual) posts)

rng:attribute.name: replyTo
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates to which previous post the current post replies or refers.

rng:attribute.name: norm
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (normalized) provides the normalized/standardized form of information present in the source text in a non-normalized form.

rng:attribute.name: orig
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (original) gives the original string or is the empty string when the element does not appear in the source text.

rng:attribute.name: lemma
rng:attribute.a:documentation: provides a lemma (base form) for the word, typically uninflected and serving both as an identifier (e.g. in dictionary contexts, as a headword), and as a basis for potential inflections.

rng:attribute.name: lemmaRef
rng:attribute.a:documentation: provides a pointer to a definition of the lemma for the word, for example in an online lexicon.

rng:attribute.name: pos
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (part of speech) indicates the part of speech assigned to a token (i.e. information on whether it is a noun, adjective, or verb), usually according to some official reference vocabulary (e.g. for German: STTS, for English: CLAWS, for Polish: NKJP, etc.).

rng:attribute.name: msd
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (morphosyntactic description) supplies morphosyntactic information for a token, usually according to some official reference vocabulary (e.g. for German: STTS-large tagset; for a feature description system designed as (pragmatically) universal, see Universal Features).

rng:attribute.name: join
rng:attribute.a:documentation: when present, provides information on whether the token in question is adjacent to another, and if so, on which side.

rng:choice.a:documentation: the token is not adjacent to another
there is no whitespace on the left side of the token
there is no whitespace on the right side of the token
there is no whitespace on either side of the token
the token overlaps with another; other devices (specifying the extent and the area of overlap) are needed to more precisely locate this token in the character stream

rng:attribute.name: ana
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (analysis) indicates one or more elements containing interpretations of the element on which the @ana attribute appears.

rng:element.name: s
rng:element.a:documentation: (s-unit) contains a sentence-like division of a text. [18.1. Linguistic Segment Categories 8.4.1. Segmentation]

sch:rule.sch:report: You may not nest one <s> element within another: use <seg> instead.

rng:element.name: cl
rng:element.a:documentation: (clause) represents a grammatical clause. [18.1. Linguistic Segment Categories]

rng:element.name: phr
rng:element.a:documentation: (phrase) represents a grammatical phrase. [18.1. Linguistic Segment Categories]

rng:element.name: w
rng:element.a:documentation: (word) represents a grammatical (not necessarily orthographic) word. [18.1. Linguistic Segment Categories 18.4.2. Lightweight Linguistic Annotation]

rng:element.name: m
rng:element.a:documentation: (morpheme) represents a grammatical morpheme. [18.1. Linguistic Segment Categories]

rng:attribute.name: baseForm
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies the morpheme's base form.

rng:element.name: c
rng:element.a:documentation: (character) represents a character. [18.1. Linguistic Segment Categories]

rng:element.name: pc
rng:element.a:documentation: (punctuation character) contains a character or string of characters regarded as constituting a single punctuation mark. [18.1.2. Below the Word Level 18.4.2. Lightweight Linguistic Annotation]

rng:attribute.name: force
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates the extent to which this punctuation mark conventionally separates words or phrases.

rng:choice.a:documentation: the punctuation mark is a word separator
the punctuation mark is not a word separator
the punctuation mark may or may not be a word separator

rng:attribute.name: unit
rng:attribute.a:documentation: provides a name for the kind of unit delimited by this punctuation mark.

rng:attribute.name: pre
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates whether this punctuation mark precedes or follows the unit it delimits.

rng:element.name: span
rng:element.a:documentation: associates an interpretative annotation directly with a span of text. [18.3. Spans and Interpretations]

sch:rule.sch:report: Only one of the attributes @target and @from may be supplied on <>.
Only one of the attributes @target and @to may be supplied on <>.
If @to is supplied on <>, @from must be supplied as well.
The attributes @to and @from on <> may each contain only a single value.

rng:attribute.name: from
rng:attribute.a:documentation: gives the identifier of the node which is the starting point of the span of text being annotated; if not accompanied by a @to attribute, gives the identifier of the node of the entire span of text being annotated.

rng:attribute.name: to
rng:attribute.a:documentation: gives the identifier of the node which is the end-point of the span of text being annotated.

rng:element.name: spanGrp
rng:element.a:documentation: (span group) collects together span tags. [18.3. Spans and Interpretations]

rng:element.name: interp
rng:element.a:documentation: (interpretation) summarizes a specific interpretative annotation which can be linked to a span of text. [18.3. Spans and Interpretations]

rng:element.name: interpGrp
rng:element.a:documentation: (interpretation group) collects together a set of related interpretations which share responsibility or type. [18.3. Spans and Interpretations]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates type of entry, in dictionaries with multiple types. Suggested values include: 1] main; 2] hom (homograph); 3] xref (cross reference); 4] affix; 5] abbr (abbreviation); 6] supplemental; 7] foreign

rng:choice.a:documentation: a main entry (default).
(homograph) groups information relating to one homograph within an entry.
(cross reference) a reduced entry whose only function is to point to another main entry (e.g. for forms of an irregular verb or for variant spellings: was pointing to be, or esthete to aesthete).
an entry for a prefix, infix, or suffix.
(abbreviation) an entry for an abbreviation.
a supplemental entry (for use in dictionaries which issue supplements to their main work in which they include updated information about entries).
an entry for a foreign word in a monolingual dictionary.

rng:attribute.name: expand
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (expand) gives an expanded form of information presented more concisely in the dictionary.

rng:attribute.name: split
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (split) gives the list of split values for a merged form.

rng:attribute.name: value
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (value) gives a value which lacks any realization in the printed source text.

rng:attribute.name: location
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (location) indicates an <anchor> element typically elsewhere in the document, but possibly in another document, which is the original location of this component.

rng:attribute.name: mergedIn
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (merged into) gives a reference to another element, where the original appears as a merged form.

rng:attribute.name: opt
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (optional) indicates whether the element is optional or not.

rng:element.name: superEntry
rng:element.a:documentation: (super entry) groups a sequence of entries within any kind of lexical resource, such as a dictionary or lexicon which function as a single unit, for example a set of homographs. [10.1. Dictionary Body and Overall Structure]

rng:element.name: entry
rng:element.a:documentation: (entry) contains a single structured entry in any kind of lexical resource, such as a dictionary or lexicon. [10.1. Dictionary Body and Overall Structure 10.2. The Structure of Dictionary Entries]

rng:element.name: entryFree
rng:element.a:documentation: (unstructured entry) contains a single unstructured entry in any kind of lexical resource, such as a dictionary or lexicon. [10.1. Dictionary Body and Overall Structure 10.2. The Structure of Dictionary Entries]

rng:element.name: hom
rng:element.a:documentation: (homograph) groups information relating to one homograph within an entry. [10.2. The Structure of Dictionary Entries]

rng:element.name: sense
rng:element.a:documentation: groups together all information relating to one word sense in a dictionary entry, for example definitions, examples, and translation equivalents. [10.2. The Structure of Dictionary Entries]

rng:attribute.name: level
rng:attribute.a:documentation: gives the nesting depth of this sense.

rng:element.name: dictScrap
rng:element.a:documentation: (dictionary scrap) encloses a part of a dictionary entry in which other phrase-level dictionary elements are freely combined. [10.1. Dictionary Body and Overall Structure 10.2. The Structure of Dictionary Entries]

rng:element.name: form
rng:element.a:documentation: (form information group) groups all the information on the written and spoken forms of one headword. [10.3.1. Information on Written and Spoken Forms]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: classifies form as simple, compound, etc. Suggested values include: 1] simple; 2] lemma; 3] variant; 4] compound; 5] derivative; 6] inflected; 7] phrase

rng:choice.a:documentation: single free lexical item
the headword itself
a variant form
word formed from simple lexical items
word derived from headword
word in other than usual dictionary form
multiple-word lexical item

rng:element.name: orth
rng:element.a:documentation: (orthographic form) gives the orthographic form of a dictionary headword. [10.3.1. Information on Written and Spoken Forms]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: gives the type of spelling.

rng:element.name: pron
rng:element.a:documentation: (pronunciation) contains the pronunciation(s) of the word. [10.3.1. Information on Written and Spoken Forms]

rng:element.name: hyph
rng:element.a:documentation: (hyphenation) contains a hyphenated form of a dictionary headword, or hyphenation information in some other form. [10.3.1. Information on Written and Spoken Forms]

rng:element.name: syll
rng:element.a:documentation: (syllabification) contains the syllabification of the headword. [10.3.1. Information on Written and Spoken Forms]

rng:element.name: stress
rng:element.a:documentation: (stress) contains the stress pattern for a dictionary headword, if given separately. [10.3.1. Information on Written and Spoken Forms]

rng:element.name: gram
rng:element.a:documentation: (grammatical information) within an entry in a dictionary or a terminological data file, contains grammatical information relating to a term, word, or form. [10.3.2. Grammatical Information]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: classifies grammatical information provided by <gram> according to some convenient and shared typology, ideally one defined in an external reference taxonomy, such as the CLARIN Concept Registry. Sample values include: 1] pos (part of speech); 2] gen (gender); 3] num (number); 4] animate; 5] proper

rng:element.name: gen
rng:element.a:documentation: (gender) identifies the morphological gender of a lexical item, as given in the dictionary. [10.3.1. Information on Written and Spoken Forms]

rng:element.name: number
rng:element.a:documentation: (number) indicates grammatical number associated with a form, as given in a dictionary. [10.3.1. Information on Written and Spoken Forms 10.3.2. Grammatical Information]

rng:element.name: case
rng:element.a:documentation: (case) contains grammatical case information given by a dictionary for a given form. [10.3.1. Information on Written and Spoken Forms]

rng:element.name: per
rng:element.a:documentation: (person) contains an indication of the grammatical person (1st, 2nd, 3rd, etc.) associated with a given inflected form in a dictionary. [10.3.1. Information on Written and Spoken Forms]

rng:element.name: tns
rng:element.a:documentation: (tense) indicates the grammatical tense associated with a given inflected form in a dictionary. [10.3.1. Information on Written and Spoken Forms]

rng:element.name: mood
rng:element.a:documentation: (mood) contains information about the grammatical mood of verbs (e.g. indicative, subjunctive, imperative). [10.3.1. Information on Written and Spoken Forms]

rng:element.name: iType
rng:element.a:documentation: (inflectional class) indicates the inflectional class associated with a lexical item. [10.3.1. Information on Written and Spoken Forms]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates the type of indicator used to specify the inflection class, when it is necessary to distinguish between the usual abbreviated indications (e.g. inv) and other kinds of indicators, such as special codes referring to conjugation patterns, etc. Sample values include: 1] abbrev; 2] verbTable

rng:element.name: gramGrp
rng:element.a:documentation: (grammatical information group) groups morpho-syntactic information about a lexical item, e.g. <pos>, <gen>, <number>, <case>, or <iType> (inflectional class). [10.3.2. Grammatical Information]

rng:element.name: pos
rng:element.a:documentation: (part of speech) indicates the part of speech assigned to a dictionary headword such as noun, verb, or adjective. [10.3.2. Grammatical Information]

rng:element.name: subc
rng:element.a:documentation: (subcategorization) contains subcategorization information (transitive/intransitive, countable/non-countable, etc.) [10.3.2. Grammatical Information]

rng:element.name: colloc
rng:element.a:documentation: (collocate) contains any sequence of words that co-occur with the headword with significant frequency. [10.3.2. Grammatical Information]

rng:element.name: def
rng:element.a:documentation: (definition) contains definition text in a dictionary entry. [10.3.3.1. Definitions]

rng:element.name: etym
rng:element.a:documentation: (etymology) encloses the etymological information in a dictionary entry. [10.3.4. Etymological Information]

rng:element.name: lang
rng:element.a:documentation: (language name) contains the name of a language mentioned in etymological or other linguistic discussion. [10.3.4. Etymological Information]

rng:element.name: usg
rng:element.a:documentation: (usage) contains usage information in a dictionary entry. [10.3.5.2. Usage Information and Other Labels]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: classifies the usage information using any convenient typology. Sample values include: 1] geo (geographic); 2] time; 3] dom (domain); 4] register (register); 5] style; 6] plev (preference level); 7] lang (language); 8] gram (grammatical); 9] syn (synonym); 10] hyper (hypernym); 11] colloc (collocation); 12] comp (complement); 13] obj (object); 14] subj (subject); 15] verb; 16] hint

rng:element.name: lbl
rng:element.a:documentation: (label) contains a label for a form, example, translation, or other piece of information, e.g. abbreviation for, contraction of, literally, approximately, synonyms:, etc. [10.3.1. Information on Written and Spoken Forms 10.3.3.2. Translation Equivalents 10.3.5.3. Cross-References to Other Entries]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: classifies the label using any convenient typology.

rng:element.name: xr
rng:element.a:documentation: (cross-reference phrase) contains a phrase, sentence, or icon referring the reader to some other location in this or another text. [10.3.5.3. Cross-References to Other Entries]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates the type of cross reference, using any convenient typology. Sample values include: 1] syn (synonym); 2] etym (etymological); 3] cf (compare or consult); 4] illus (illustration)

rng:element.name: oRef
rng:element.a:documentation: (orthographic-form reference) in a dictionary example, indicates a reference to the orthographic form(s) of the headword. [10.4. Headword and Pronunciation References]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates the kind of typographic modification made to the headword in the reference. Sample values include: 1] cap (capital); 2] noHyph (no hyphen)

rng:element.name: pRef
rng:element.a:documentation: (pronunciation reference) in a dictionary example, indicates a reference to the pronunciation(s) of the headword. [10.4. Headword and Pronunciation References]

rng:attribute.name: defective
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates whether the passage being quoted is defective, i.e. incomplete through loss or damage.

rng:attribute.name: class
rng:attribute.a:documentation: identifies the text types or classifications applicable to this item by pointing to other elements or resources defining the classification concerned.

rng:element.name: msDesc
rng:element.a:documentation: (manuscript description) contains a description of a single identifiable manuscript or other text-bearing object such as an early printed book. [11.1. Overview]

sch:report.test: preceding-sibling::*[ name(.) eq $gi ] and not( following-sibling::*[ name(.) eq $gi ] )

sch:rule.sch:report: Only one <> is allowed as a child of <>.

rng:element.name: catchwords
rng:element.a:documentation: (catchwords) describes the system used to ensure correct ordering of the quires or similar making up a codex, incunable, or other object typically by means of annotations at the foot of the page. [11.3.7. Catchwords, Signatures, Secundo Folio]

sch:rule.sch:assert: The <> element should not be used outside of <msDesc>.

rng:element.name: dimensions
rng:element.a:documentation: (dimensions) contains a dimensional specification. [11.3.4. Dimensions]

sch:rule.sch:report: The element <> may appear once only.
The element <> may appear once only.
The element <> may appear once only.

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates which aspect of the object is being measured. Sample values include: 1] leaves; 2] ruled; 3] pricked; 4] written; 5] miniatures; 6] binding; 7] box

rng:element.name: dim
rng:element.a:documentation: contains any single measurement forming part of a dimensional specification of some sort. [11.3.4. Dimensions]

rng:element.name: height
rng:element.a:documentation: (height) contains a measurement measured along the axis at a right angle to the bottom of the object. [11.3.4. Dimensions]

rng:element.name: depth
rng:element.a:documentation: (depth) contains a measurement from the front to the back of an object, perpendicular to the measurement given by the <width> element. [11.3.4. Dimensions]

rng:element.name: width
rng:element.a:documentation: (width) contains a measurement of an object along the axis parallel to its bottom, e.g. perpendicular to the spine of a book or codex. [11.3.4. Dimensions]

rng:element.name: heraldry
rng:element.a:documentation: (heraldry) contains a heraldic formula or phrase, typically found as part of a blazon, coat of arms, etc. [11.3.8. Heraldry]

rng:element.name: locus
rng:element.a:documentation: (locus) defines a location within a manuscript, manuscript part, or other object typically as a (possibly discontinuous) sequence of folio references. [11.3.5. References to Locations within a Manuscript]

rng:attribute.name: scheme
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (scheme) identifies the foliation scheme in terms of which the location is being specified by pointing to some <foliation> element defining it, or to some other equivalent resource.

rng:attribute.name: from
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (from) specifies the starting point of the location in a normalized form, typically a page number.

rng:attribute.name: to
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (to) specifies the end-point of the location in a normalized form, typically as a page number.

rng:element.name: locusGrp
rng:element.a:documentation: (locus group) groups a number of locations which together form a distinct but discontinuous item within a manuscript, manuscript part, or other object. [11.3.5. References to Locations within a Manuscript]

rng:attribute.name: scheme
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (scheme) identifies the foliation scheme in terms of which all the locations contained by the group are specified by pointing to some <foliation> element defining it, or to some other equivalent resource.

rng:element.name: material
rng:element.a:documentation: (material) contains a word or phrase describing the material of which the object being described is composed. [11.3.2. Material and Object Type]

rng:attribute.name: function
rng:attribute.a:documentation: describes the function or use of the material in relation to the object as a whole. Sample values include: 1] binding; 2] endband; 3] slipcase; 4] support; 5] tie

rng:attribute.name: target
rng:attribute.a:documentation: identifies one or more elements to which the metamark applies.

rng:element.name: objectType
rng:element.a:documentation: (object type) contains a word or phrase describing the type of object being referred to. [11.3.2. Material and Object Type]

rng:element.name: origDate
rng:element.a:documentation: (origin date) contains any form of date, used to identify the date of origin for a manuscript, manuscript part, or other object. [11.3.1. Origination]

rng:element.name: origPlace
rng:element.a:documentation: (origin place) contains any form of place name, used to identify the place of origin for a manuscript, manuscript part, or other object. [11.3.1. Origination]

rng:element.name: secFol
rng:element.a:documentation: (second folio) marks the word or words taken from a fixed point in a codex (typically the beginning of the second leaf) in order to provide a unique identifier for it. [11.3.7. Catchwords, Signatures, Secundo Folio]

sch:rule.sch:assert: The <> element should not be used outside of <msDesc>.

rng:element.name: signatures
rng:element.a:documentation: (signatures) contains discussion of the leaf or quire signatures found within a codex or similar object. [11.3.7. Catchwords, Signatures, Secundo Folio]

sch:rule.sch:assert: The <> element should not be used outside of <msDesc>.

rng:element.name: stamp
rng:element.a:documentation: (stamp) contains a word or phrase describing a stamp or similar device. [11.3.3. Watermarks and Stamps]

rng:element.name: watermark
rng:element.a:documentation: (watermark) contains a word or phrase describing a watermark or similar device. [11.3.3. Watermarks and Stamps]

rng:element.name: msIdentifier
rng:element.a:documentation: (manuscript identifier) contains the information required to identify the manuscript or similar object being described. [11.4. The Manuscript Identifier]

sch:report.test: not( parent::tei:msPart ) and ( child::*[1]/self::idno or child::*[1]/self::altIdentifier or normalize-space(.) eq '')

sch:rule.sch:report: An <msIdentifier> must contain either a <repository> or <location>.

rng:element.name: institution
rng:element.a:documentation: (institution) contains the name of an organization such as a university or library, with which a manuscript or other object is identified, generally its holding institution. [11.4. The Manuscript Identifier]

rng:element.name: repository
rng:element.a:documentation: (repository) contains the name of a repository within which manuscripts or other objects are stored, possibly forming part of an institution. [11.4. The Manuscript Identifier]

rng:element.name: collection
rng:element.a:documentation: (collection) contains the name of a collection of manuscripts or other objects, not necessarily located within a single repository. [11.4. The Manuscript Identifier]

rng:element.name: altIdentifier
rng:element.a:documentation: (alternative identifier) contains an alternative or former structured identifier used for a manuscript or other object, such as a former catalogue number. [11.4. The Manuscript Identifier]

rng:element.name: msName
rng:element.a:documentation: (manuscript name) contains a proper noun or noun phrase used for a manuscript, or other object, as opposed to a formal identification number or classmark. [11.4. The Manuscript Identifier]

rng:element.name: colophon
rng:element.a:documentation: (colophon) contains the colophon of an item: that is, a statement providing information regarding the date, place, agency, or reason for production of the manuscript or other object. [11.6.1. The msItem and msItemStruct Elements]

rng:element.name: explicit
rng:element.a:documentation: (explicit) contains the explicit of a item, that is, the closing words of the text proper, exclusive of any rubric or colophon which might follow it. [11.6.1. The msItem and msItemStruct Elements]

rng:element.name: filiation
rng:element.a:documentation: (filiation) contains information concerning the manuscript or other object's filiation, i.e. its relationship to other surviving manuscripts or other objects of the same text or contents, its protographs, antigraphs and apographs. [11.6.1. The msItem and msItemStruct Elements]

rng:element.name: finalRubric
rng:element.a:documentation: (final rubric) contains the string of words that denotes the end of a text division, often with an assertion as to its author and title, usually set off from the text itself by red ink, by a different size or type of script, or by some other such visual device. [11.6.1. The msItem and msItemStruct Elements]

rng:element.name: incipit
rng:element.a:documentation: contains the incipit of a manuscript or similar object item, that is the opening words of the text proper, exclusive of any rubric which might precede it, of sufficient length to identify the work uniquely; such incipits were, in former times, frequently used a means of reference to a work, in place of a title. [11.6.1. The msItem and msItemStruct Elements]

rng:element.name: msContents
rng:element.a:documentation: (manuscript contents) describes the intellectual content of a manuscript, manuscript part, or other object either as a series of paragraphs or as a series of structured manuscript items. [11.6. Intellectual Content]

rng:element.name: msItem
rng:element.a:documentation: (manuscript item) describes an individual work or item within the intellectual content of a manuscript, manuscript part, or other object. [11.6.1. The msItem and msItemStruct Elements]

rng:element.name: msItemStruct
rng:element.a:documentation: (structured manuscript item) contains a structured description for an individual work or item within the intellectual content of a manuscript, manuscript part, or other object. [11.6.1. The msItem and msItemStruct Elements]

rng:element.name: rubric
rng:element.a:documentation: (rubric) contains the text of any rubric or heading attached to a particular manuscript item, that is, a string of words through which a manuscript or other object signals the beginning of a text division, often with an assertion as to its author and title, which is in some way set off from the text itself, typically in red ink, or by use of different size or type of script, or some other such visual device. [11.6.1. The msItem and msItemStruct Elements]

rng:element.name: summary
rng:element.a:documentation: contains an overview of the available information concerning some aspect of an item or object (for example, its intellectual content, history, layout, typography etc.) as a complement or alternative to the more detailed information carried by more specific elements. [11.6. Intellectual Content]

rng:element.name: physDesc
rng:element.a:documentation: (physical description) contains a full physical description of a manuscript, manuscript part, or other object optionally subdivided using more specialized elements from the model.physDescPart class. [11.7. Physical Description]

rng:element.name: objectDesc
rng:element.a:documentation: (object description) contains a description of the physical components making up the object which is being described. [11.7.1. Object Description]

rng:attribute.name: form
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (form) a short project-specific name identifying the physical form of the carrier, for example as a codex, roll, fragment, partial leaf, cutting etc.

rng:element.name: supportDesc
rng:element.a:documentation: (support description) groups elements describing the physical support for the written part of a manuscript or other object. [11.7.1. Object Description]

rng:attribute.name: material
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (material) a short project-defined name for the material composing the majority of the support. Suggested values include: 1] paper; 2] parch (parchment); 3] mixed

rng:choice.a:documentation: (parchment)

rng:element.name: support
rng:element.a:documentation: (support) contains a description of the materials etc. which make up the physical support for the written part of a manuscript or other object. [11.7.1. Object Description]

rng:element.name: collation
rng:element.a:documentation: (collation) contains a description of how the leaves, bifolia, or similar objects are physically arranged. [11.7.1. Object Description]

rng:element.name: foliation
rng:element.a:documentation: (foliation) describes the numbering system or systems used to count the leaves or pages in a codex or similar object. [11.7.1.4. Foliation]

rng:element.name: condition
rng:element.a:documentation: (condition) contains a description of the physical condition of the manuscript or object. [11.7.1.5. Condition]

rng:element.name: layoutDesc
rng:element.a:documentation: (layout description) collects the set of layout descriptions applicable to a manuscript or other object. [11.7.2. Writing, Decoration, and Other Notations]

rng:element.name: layout
rng:element.a:documentation: (layout) describes how text is laid out on the page or surface of the object, including information about any ruling, pricking, or other evidence of page-preparation techniques. [11.7.2. Writing, Decoration, and Other Notations]

rng:attribute.name: columns
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (columns) specifies the number of columns per page.

rng:attribute.name: streams
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (textual streams) indicates the number of streams per page, each of which contains an independent textual stream.

rng:attribute.name: ruledLines
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (ruled lines) specifies the number of ruled lines per column.

rng:attribute.name: writtenLines
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (written lines) specifies the number of written lines per column.

rng:element.name: handDesc
rng:element.a:documentation: (description of hands) contains a description of all the different hands used in a manuscript or other object. [11.7.2. Writing, Decoration, and Other Notations]

rng:attribute.name: hands
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (hands) specifies the number of distinct hands identified within the manuscript.

rng:element.name: typeDesc
rng:element.a:documentation: (typeface description) contains a description of the typefaces or other aspects of the printing of an incunable or other printed source. [11.7.2.1. Writing]

rng:element.name: typeNote
rng:element.a:documentation: (typographic note) describes a particular font or other significant typographic feature distinguished within the description of a printed resource. [11.7.2. Writing, Decoration, and Other Notations]

rng:element.name: scriptDesc
rng:element.a:documentation: (script description) contains a description of the scripts used in a manuscript or other object. [11.7.2.1. Writing]

rng:element.name: musicNotation
rng:element.a:documentation: (music notation) contains description of type of musical notation. [11.7.2. Writing, Decoration, and Other Notations]

rng:element.name: decoDesc
rng:element.a:documentation: (decoration description) contains a description of the decoration of a manuscript or other object, either as in paragraphs, or as one or more <decoNote> elements. [11.7.3. Bindings, Seals, and Additional Material]

rng:element.name: decoNote
rng:element.a:documentation: (note on decoration) contains a note describing either a decorative component of a manuscript or other object, or a fairly homogenous class of such components. [11.7.3. Bindings, Seals, and Additional Material]

rng:element.name: additions
rng:element.a:documentation: (additions) contains a description of any significant additions found within a manuscript or other object, such as marginalia or other annotations. [11.7.2. Writing, Decoration, and Other Notations]

rng:element.name: bindingDesc
rng:element.a:documentation: (binding description) describes the present and former bindings of a manuscript or other object, either as a series of paragraphs or as a series of distinct <binding> elements, one for each binding of the manuscript. [11.7.3.1. Binding Descriptions]

rng:element.name: binding
rng:element.a:documentation: (binding) contains a description of one binding, i.e. type of covering, boards, etc. applied to a manuscript or other object. [11.7.3.1. Binding Descriptions]

rng:attribute.name: contemporary
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (contemporary) specifies whether or not the binding is contemporary with the majority of its contents.

rng:element.name: sealDesc
rng:element.a:documentation: (seal description) describes the seals or similar items related to the object described, either as a series of paragraphs or as a series of <seal> elements. [11.7.3.2. Seals]

rng:element.name: seal
rng:element.a:documentation: (seal) contains a description of one seal or similar applied to the object described. [11.7.3.2. Seals]

rng:attribute.name: contemporary
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (contemporary) specifies whether or not the seal is contemporary with the item to which it is affixed

rng:element.name: accMat
rng:element.a:documentation: (accompanying material) contains details of any significant additional material which may be closely associated with the manuscript or object being described, such as non-contemporaneous documents or fragments bound in with it at some earlier historical period. [11.7.3.3. Accompanying Material]

rng:element.name: history
rng:element.a:documentation: (history) groups elements describing the full history of a manuscript, manuscript part, or other object. [11.8. History]

rng:element.name: origin
rng:element.a:documentation: (origin) contains any descriptive or other information concerning the origin of a manuscript, manuscript part, or other object. [11.8. History]

rng:element.name: provenance
rng:element.a:documentation: (provenance) contains any descriptive or other information concerning a single identifiable episode during the history of a manuscript, manuscript part, or other object after its creation but before its acquisition. [11.8. History]

rng:element.name: acquisition
rng:element.a:documentation: (acquisition) contains any descriptive or other information concerning the process by which a manuscript or manuscript part or other object entered the holding institution. [11.8. History]

rng:element.name: additional
rng:element.a:documentation: (additional) groups additional information, combining bibliographic information about a manuscript or other object, or surrogate copies of it, with curatorial or administrative information. [11.9. Additional Information]

rng:element.name: adminInfo
rng:element.a:documentation: (administrative information) contains information about the present custody and availability of the manuscript or other object, and also about the record description itself. [11.9.1. Administrative Information]

rng:element.name: recordHist
rng:element.a:documentation: (recorded history) provides information about the source and revision status of the parent manuscript or object description itself. [11.9.1. Administrative Information]

rng:element.name: source
rng:element.a:documentation: (source) describes the original source for the information contained with a manuscript or object description. [11.9.1.1. Record History]

rng:element.name: custodialHist
rng:element.a:documentation: (custodial history) contains a description of a manuscript or other object's custodial history, either as running prose or as a series of dated custodial events. [11.9.1.2. Availability and Custodial History]

rng:element.name: custEvent
rng:element.a:documentation: (custodial event) describes a single event during the custodial history of a manuscript or other object. [11.9.1.2. Availability and Custodial History]

rng:element.name: surrogates
rng:element.a:documentation: (surrogates) contains information about any representations of the manuscript or other object being described which may exist in the holding institution or elsewhere. [11.9. Additional Information]

rng:element.name: msPart
rng:element.a:documentation: (manuscript part) contains information about an originally distinct manuscript or part of a manuscript, which is now part of a composite manuscript. [11.10. Manuscript Parts]

rng:element.name: msFrag
rng:element.a:documentation: (manuscript fragment) contains information about a fragment described in relation to a prior context, typically as a description of a virtual reconstruction of a manuscript or other object whose fragments were catalogued separately. [11.11. Manuscript Fragments]

rng:attribute.name: facs
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (facsimile) points to one or more images, portions of an image, or surfaces which correspond to the current element.

rng:attribute.name: change
rng:attribute.a:documentation: points to one or more <change> elements documenting a state or revision campaign to which the element bearing this attribute and its children have been assigned by the encoder.

rng:attribute.name: start
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates the element within a transcription of the text containing at least the start of the writing represented by this zone or surface.

rng:attribute.name: ulx
rng:attribute.a:documentation: gives the x coordinate value for the upper left corner of a rectangular space.

rng:attribute.name: uly
rng:attribute.a:documentation: gives the y coordinate value for the upper left corner of a rectangular space.

rng:attribute.name: lrx
rng:attribute.a:documentation: gives the x coordinate value for the lower right corner of a rectangular space.

rng:attribute.name: lry
rng:attribute.a:documentation: gives the y coordinate value for the lower right corner of a rectangular space.

rng:attribute.name: points
rng:attribute.a:documentation: identifies a two or three dimensional area by means of a series of pairs of numbers, each of which gives the x,y, or z coordinates of a point on a line enclosing the area.

rng:element.name: facsimile
rng:element.a:documentation: contains a representation of some written source in the form of a set of images rather than as transcribed or encoded text. [12.1. Digital Facsimiles]

sch:rule.sch:report: A <facsimile> element represents a text with images, thus transcribed text should not be present within it.

rng:element.name: sourceDoc
rng:element.a:documentation: contains a transcription or other representation of a single source document potentially forming part of a dossier génétique or collection of sources. [12.1. Digital Facsimiles 12.2.2. Embedded Transcription]

rng:element.name: surface
rng:element.a:documentation: defines a written surface as a two-dimensional or three-dimensional coordinate space, optionally grouping one or more graphic representations of that space, zones of interest within that space, and, when using an embedded transcription approach, transcriptions of the writing within them. [12.1. Digital Facsimiles 12.2.2. Embedded Transcription]

rng:attribute.name: attachment
rng:attribute.a:documentation: describes the method by which this surface is or was connected to the main surface. Sample values include: 1] glued; 2] pinned; 3] sewn

rng:attribute.name: flipping
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates whether the surface is attached and folded in such a way as to provide two writing surfaces.

rng:element.name: surfaceGrp
rng:element.a:documentation: (surface group) defines any kind of useful grouping of written surfaces, for example the recto and verso of a single leaf, which the encoder wishes to treat as a single unit. [12.1. Digital Facsimiles]

rng:element.name: zone
rng:element.a:documentation: defines any two-dimensional or three-dimensional area within a <surface> element. [12.1. Digital Facsimiles 12.2.2. Embedded Transcription]

rng:attribute.name: rotate
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates the amount by which this zone has been rotated clockwise, with respect to the normal orientation of the parent <surface> element as implied by the dimensions given in the <msDesc> element or by the coordinates of the <surface> itself. The orientation is expressed in arc degrees.

rng:element.name: path
rng:element.a:documentation: (path) defines any line passing through two or more points within a <surface> element. [12.1. Digital Facsimiles 12.2.2. Embedded Transcription]

sch:rule.sch:report: The first and last elements of this path are the same. To specify a closed polygon, use the <zone> element rather than the <path> element.

rng:attribute.name: points
rng:attribute.a:documentation: identifies a line within the container or bounding box specified by the parent element by means of a series of two or more pairs of numbers, each of which gives the x,y coordinates of a point on the line.

rng:element.name: addSpan
rng:element.a:documentation: (added span of text) marks the beginning of a longer sequence of text added by an author, scribe, annotator or corrector (see also <add>). [12.3.1.4. Additions and Deletions]

sch:rule.sch:assert: The @spanTo attribute of <> is required.
L'attribut spanTo est requis.

rng:element.name: damage
rng:element.a:documentation: (damage) contains an area of damage to the text witness. [12.3.3.1. Damage, Illegibility, and Supplied Text]

rng:element.name: damageSpan
rng:element.a:documentation: (damaged span of text) marks the beginning of a longer sequence of text which is damaged in some way but still legible. [12.3.3.1. Damage, Illegibility, and Supplied Text]

sch:rule.sch:assert: The @spanTo attribute of <> is required.
L'attribut spanTo est requis.

rng:element.name: delSpan
rng:element.a:documentation: (deleted span of text) marks the beginning of a longer sequence of text deleted, marked as deleted, or otherwise signaled as superfluous or spurious by an author, scribe, annotator, or corrector. [12.3.1.4. Additions and Deletions]

sch:rule.sch:assert: The @spanTo attribute of <> is required.
L'attribut spanTo est requis.

rng:element.name: ex
rng:element.a:documentation: (editorial expansion) contains a sequence of letters added by an editor or transcriber when expanding an abbreviation. [12.3.1.2. Abbreviation and Expansion]

rng:element.name: fw
rng:element.a:documentation: (forme work) contains a running head (e.g. a header, footer), catchword, or similar material appearing on the current page. [12.6. Headers, Footers, and Similar Matter]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: classifies the material encoded according to some useful typology. Sample values include: 1] header; 2] footer; 3] pageNum (page number); 4] lineNum (line number); 5] sig (signature); 6] catch (catchword)

rng:element.name: handNotes
rng:element.a:documentation: contains one or more <handNote> elements documenting the different hands identified within the source texts. [12.3.2.1. Document Hands]

rng:element.name: handShift
rng:element.a:documentation: (handwriting shift) marks the beginning of a sequence of text written in a new hand, or the beginning of a scribal stint. [12.3.2.1. Document Hands]

rng:attribute.name: new
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates a <handNote> element describing the hand concerned.

rng:element.name: am
rng:element.a:documentation: (abbreviation marker) contains a sequence of letters or signs present in an abbreviation which are omitted or replaced in the expanded form of the abbreviation. [12.3.1.2. Abbreviation and Expansion]

rng:element.name: restore
rng:element.a:documentation: (restore) indicates restoration of text to an earlier state by cancellation of an editorial or authorial marking or instruction. [12.3.1.6. Cancellation of Deletions and Other Markings]

rng:element.name: space
rng:element.a:documentation: (space) indicates the location of a significant space in the text. [12.4.1. Space]

rng:attribute.name: resp
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (responsible party) (responsible party) indicates the individual responsible for identifying and measuring the space.

rng:attribute.name: dim
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (dimension) indicates whether the space is horizontal or vertical.

rng:choice.a:documentation: the space is horizontal.
the space is vertical.

rng:element.name: subst
rng:element.a:documentation: (substitution) groups one or more deletions (or surplus text) with one or more additions when the combination is to be regarded as a single intervention in the text. [12.3.1.5. Substitutions]

sch:rule.sch:assert: <> must have at least one child <add> and at least one child <del> or <surplus>.

rng:element.name: substJoin
rng:element.a:documentation: (substitution join) identifies a series of possibly fragmented additions, deletions, or other revisions on a manuscript that combine to make up a single intervention in the text. [12.3.1.5. Substitutions]

rng:element.name: supplied
rng:element.a:documentation: (supplied) signifies text supplied by the transcriber or editor for any reason; for example because the original cannot be read due to physical damage, or because of an obvious omission by the author or scribe. [12.3.3.1. Damage, Illegibility, and Supplied Text]

rng:attribute.name: reason
rng:attribute.a:documentation: one or more words indicating why the text has had to be supplied, e.g. overbinding, faded-ink, lost-folio, omitted-in-original.

rng:element.name: surplus
rng:element.a:documentation: (surplus) marks text present in the source which the editor believes to be superfluous or redundant. [12.3.3.1. Damage, Illegibility, and Supplied Text]

rng:attribute.name: reason
rng:attribute.a:documentation: one or more words indicating why this text is believed to be superfluous, e.g. repeated, interpolated etc.

rng:element.name: secl
rng:element.a:documentation: (secluded text) marks text present in the source which the editor believes to be genuine but out of its original place (which is unknown). [12.3.1.7. Text Omitted from or Supplied in the Transcription]

rng:attribute.name: reason
rng:attribute.a:documentation: one or more words indicating why this text has been secluded, e.g. interpolated etc.

rng:element.name: line
rng:element.a:documentation: contains the transcription of a topographic line in the source document. [12.2.2. Embedded Transcription]

rng:element.name: listTranspose
rng:element.a:documentation: supplies a list of transpositions, each of which is indicated at some point in a document typically by means of metamarks. [12.3.4.5. Transpositions]

rng:element.name: metamark
rng:element.a:documentation: contains or describes any kind of graphic or written signal within a document the function of which is to determine how it should be read rather than forming part of the actual content of the document. [12.3.4.2. Metamarks]

rng:attribute.name: function
rng:attribute.a:documentation: describes the function (for example status, insertion, deletion, transposition) of the metamark.

rng:attribute.name: target
rng:attribute.a:documentation: identifies one or more elements to which the metamark applies.

rng:element.name: mod
rng:element.a:documentation: represents any kind of modification identified within a single document. [12.3.4.1. Generic Modification]

rng:element.name: redo
rng:element.a:documentation: indicates one or more cancelled interventions in a document which have subsequently been marked as reaffirmed or repeated. [12.3.4.4. Confirmation, Cancellation, and Reinstatement of Modifications]

rng:attribute.name: target
rng:attribute.a:documentation: points to one or more elements representing the interventions which are being reasserted.

rng:element.name: retrace
rng:element.a:documentation: contains a sequence of writing which has been retraced, for example by over-inking, to clarify or fix it. [12.3.4.3. Fixation and Clarification]

rng:element.name: transpose
rng:element.a:documentation: describes a single textual transposition as an ordered list of at least two pointers specifying the order in which the elements indicated should be re-combined. [12.3.4.5. Transpositions]

rng:element.name: undo
rng:element.a:documentation: indicates one or more marked-up interventions in a document which have subsequently been marked for cancellation. [12.3.4.4. Confirmation, Cancellation, and Reinstatement of Modifications]

rng:attribute.name: target
rng:attribute.a:documentation: points to one or more elements representing the interventions which are to be reverted or undone.

rng:attribute.name: wit
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (witness or witnesses) contains a space-delimited list of one or more sigla indicating the witnesses to this reading beginning or ending at this point.

rng:attribute.name: wit
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (witness or witnesses) contains a space-delimited list of one or more pointers indicating the witnesses which attest to a given reading.

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: classifies the reading according to some useful typology. Sample values include: 1] substantive (substantive); 2] orthographic (orthographic)

rng:attribute.name: cause
rng:attribute.a:documentation: classifies the cause for the variant reading, according to any appropriate typology of possible origins. Sample values include: 1] homeoteleuton; 2] homeoarchy; 3] paleographicConfusion; 4] haplography; 5] dittography; 6] falseEmendation

rng:attribute.name: varSeq
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (variant sequence) provides a number indicating the position of this reading in a sequence, when there is reason to presume a sequence to the variants.

rng:attribute.name: require
rng:attribute.a:documentation: points to other readings that are required when adopting the current reading or lemma.

rng:element.name: app
rng:element.a:documentation: (apparatus entry) contains one entry in a critical apparatus, with an optional lemma and usually one or more readings or notes on the relevant passage. [13.1.1. The Apparatus Entry]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: classifies the variation contained in this element according to some convenient typology.

rng:attribute.name: from
rng:attribute.a:documentation: identifies the beginning of the lemma in the base text.

rng:attribute.name: to
rng:attribute.a:documentation: identifies the endpoint of the lemma in the base text.

rng:attribute.name: loc
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (location) indicates the location of the variation, when the location-referenced method of apparatus markup is used.

rng:element.name: listApp
rng:element.a:documentation: (list of apparatus entries) contains a list of apparatus entries. [13.2. Linking the Apparatus to the Text]

rng:element.name: lem
rng:element.a:documentation: (lemma) contains the lemma, or base text, of a textual variation. [13.1. The Apparatus Entry, Readings, and Witnesses]

rng:element.name: rdg
rng:element.a:documentation: (reading) contains a single reading within a textual variation. [13.1. The Apparatus Entry, Readings, and Witnesses]

rng:element.name: rdgGrp
rng:element.a:documentation: (reading group) within a textual variation, groups two or more readings perceived to have a genetic relationship or other affinity. [13.1. The Apparatus Entry, Readings, and Witnesses]

sch:rule.sch:assert: Only one <lem> element may appear within a <rdgGrp>.

rng:element.name: witDetail
rng:element.a:documentation: (witness detail) gives further information about a particular witness, or witnesses, to a particular reading. [13.1. The Apparatus Entry, Readings, and Witnesses]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: describes the type of information given about the witness.

rng:attribute.name: wit
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (witnesses) indicates the sigil or sigla identifying the witness or witnesses to which the detail refers.

rng:element.name: wit
rng:element.a:documentation: (wit) contains a list of one or more sigla of witnesses attesting a given reading, in a textual variation. [13.1.4. Witness Information]

rng:element.name: listWit
rng:element.a:documentation: (witness list) lists definitions for all the witnesses referred to by a critical apparatus, optionally grouped hierarchically. [13.1. The Apparatus Entry, Readings, and Witnesses]

rng:element.name: witness
rng:element.a:documentation: (witness) contains either a description of a single witness referred to within the critical apparatus, or a list of witnesses which is to be referred to by a single sigil. [13.1. The Apparatus Entry, Readings, and Witnesses]

rng:element.name: witStart
rng:element.a:documentation: (fragmented witness start) indicates the beginning, or resumption, of the text of a fragmentary witness. [13.1.5. Fragmentary Witnesses]

rng:element.name: witEnd
rng:element.a:documentation: (fragmented witness end) indicates the end, or suspension, of the text of a fragmentary witness. [13.1.5. Fragmentary Witnesses]

rng:element.name: lacunaStart
rng:element.a:documentation: (lacuna start) indicates the beginning of a lacuna in the text of a mostly complete textual witness. [13.1.5. Fragmentary Witnesses]

rng:element.name: lacunaEnd
rng:element.a:documentation: (lacuna end) indicates the end of a lacuna in a mostly complete textual witness. [13.1.5. Fragmentary Witnesses]

rng:element.name: variantEncoding
rng:element.a:documentation: (variant encoding) declares the method used to encode text-critical variants. [13.1.1. The Apparatus Entry]

rng:attribute.name: method
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates which method is used to encode the apparatus of variants.

rng:choice.a:documentation: apparatus uses line numbers or other canonical reference scheme referenced in a base text.
apparatus indicates the precise locations of the beginning and ending of each lemma relative to a base text.
alternate readings of a passage are given in parallel in the text; no notion of a base text is necessary.

rng:attribute.name: location
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates whether the apparatus appears within the running text or external to it.

rng:choice.a:documentation: apparatus appears within the running text.
apparatus appears outside the base text.

sch:rule.sch:report: The @location value "external" is inconsistent with the parallel-segmentation method of apparatus markup.

rng:attribute.name: when-custom
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies the value of a date or time in some custom standard form.

rng:attribute.name: notBefore-custom
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the earliest possible date for the event in some custom standard form.

rng:attribute.name: notAfter-custom
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the latest possible date for the event in some custom standard form.

rng:attribute.name: from-custom
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates the starting point of the period in some custom standard form.

rng:attribute.name: to-custom
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates the ending point of the period in some custom standard form.

rng:attribute.name: datingPoint
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies a pointer to some location defining a named point in time with reference to which the datable item is understood to have occurred.

rng:attribute.name: datingMethod
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies a pointer to a <calendar> element or other means of interpreting the values of the custom dating attributes.

rng:attribute.name: when-iso
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies the value of a date or time in a standard form.

rng:attribute.name: notBefore-iso
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the earliest possible date for the event in standard form, e.g. yyyy-mm-dd.

rng:attribute.name: notAfter-iso
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the latest possible date for the event in standard form, e.g. yyyy-mm-dd.

rng:attribute.name: from-iso
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates the starting point of the period in standard form.

rng:attribute.name: to-iso
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates the ending point of the period in standard form.

rng:element.name: orgName
rng:element.a:documentation: (organization name) contains an organizational name. [14.2.2. Organizational Names]

rng:element.name: persName
rng:element.a:documentation: (personal name) contains a proper noun or proper-noun phrase referring to a person, possibly including one or more of the person's forenames, surnames, honorifics, added names, etc. [14.2.1. Personal Names]

rng:element.name: surname
rng:element.a:documentation: (surname) contains a family (inherited) name, as opposed to a given, baptismal, or nick name. [14.2.1. Personal Names]

rng:element.name: forename
rng:element.a:documentation: (forename) contains a forename, given or baptismal name. [14.2.1. Personal Names]

rng:element.name: genName
rng:element.a:documentation: (generational name component) contains a name component used to distinguish otherwise similar names on the basis of the relative ages or generations of the persons named. [14.2.1. Personal Names]

rng:element.name: nameLink
rng:element.a:documentation: (name link) contains a connecting phrase or link used within a name but not regarded as part of it, such as van der or of. [14.2.1. Personal Names]

rng:element.name: addName
rng:element.a:documentation: (additional name) contains an additional name component, such as a nickname, epithet, or alias, or any other descriptive phrase used within a personal name. [14.2.1. Personal Names]

rng:element.name: roleName
rng:element.a:documentation: (role name) contains a name component which indicates that the referent has a particular role or position in society, such as an official title or rank. [14.2.1. Personal Names]

rng:element.name: placeName
rng:element.a:documentation: (place name) contains an absolute or relative place name. [14.2.3. Place Names]

rng:element.name: bloc
rng:element.a:documentation: (bloc) contains the name of a geo-political unit consisting of two or more nation states or countries. [14.2.3. Place Names]

rng:element.name: country
rng:element.a:documentation: (country) contains the name of a geo-political unit, such as a nation, country, colony, or commonwealth, larger than or administratively superior to a region and smaller than a bloc. [14.2.3. Place Names]

rng:element.name: region
rng:element.a:documentation: (region) contains the name of an administrative unit such as a state, province, or county, larger than a settlement, but smaller than a country. [14.2.3. Place Names]

rng:element.name: settlement
rng:element.a:documentation: (settlement) contains the name of a settlement such as a city, town, or village identified as a single geo-political or administrative unit. [14.2.3. Place Names]

rng:element.name: district
rng:element.a:documentation: (district) contains the name of any kind of subdivision of a settlement, such as a parish, ward, or other administrative or geographic unit. [14.2.3. Place Names]

rng:element.name: offset
rng:element.a:documentation: (offset) marks that part of a relative temporal or spatial expression which indicates the direction of the offset between the two place names, dates, or times involved in the expression. [14.2.3. Place Names]

rng:element.name: geogName
rng:element.a:documentation: (geographical name) identifies a name associated with some geographical feature such as Windrush Valley or Mount Sinai. [14.2.3. Place Names]

rng:element.name: geogFeat
rng:element.a:documentation: (geographical feature name) contains a common noun identifying some geographical feature contained within a geographic name, such as valley, mount, etc. [14.2.3. Place Names]

rng:element.name: eventName
rng:element.a:documentation: (name of an event) contains a proper noun or noun phrase used to refer to an event. [14.2.4. Event Names]

rng:element.name: affiliation
rng:element.a:documentation: (affiliation) contains an informal description of a person's present or past affiliation with some organization, for example an employer or sponsor. [16.2.2. The Participant Description]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: characterizes the element in some sense, using any convenient classification scheme or typology. Sample values include: 1] sponsor; 2] recommend; 3] discredit; 4] pledged

rng:element.name: age
rng:element.a:documentation: (age) specifies the age of a person. [14.3.2.1. Personal Characteristics]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: characterizes the element in some sense, using any convenient classification scheme or typology. Sample values include: 1] western; 2] sui; 3] subjective; 4] objective; 5] inWorld (in world); 6] chronological; 7] biological; 8] psychological; 9] functional

rng:attribute.name: value
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies a numeric code representing the age or age group.

rng:element.name: birth
rng:element.a:documentation: (birth) contains information about a person's birth, such as its date and place. [16.2.2. The Participant Description]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: characterizes the element in some sense, using any convenient classification scheme or typology. Sample values include: 1] caesarean (caesarean section); 2] vaginal (vaginal delivery); 3] exNihilo (ex nihilo); 4] incorporated; 5] founded; 6] established

rng:element.name: climate
rng:element.a:documentation: (climate) contains information about the physical climate of a place. [14.3.4.3. States, Traits, and Events]

rng:element.name: death
rng:element.a:documentation: (death) contains information about a person's death, such as its date and place. [16.2.2. The Participant Description]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: characterizes the element in some sense, using any convenient classification scheme or typology. Sample values include: 1] proclaimed; 2] assumed; 3] verified; 4] clinical; 5] brain; 6] natural; 7] unnatural; 8] fragmentation; 9] dissolution

rng:element.name: education
rng:element.a:documentation: (education) contains a description of the educational experience of a person. [16.2.2. The Participant Description]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: characterizes the element in some sense, using any convenient classification scheme or typology. Sample values include: 1] primary; 2] secondary; 3] undergraduate; 4] graduate; 5] residency; 6] apprenticeship

rng:element.name: event
rng:element.a:documentation: (event) contains data relating to anything of significance that happens in time. [14.3.1. Basic Principles]

rng:element.name: faith
rng:element.a:documentation: (faith) specifies the faith, religion, or belief set of a person. [14.3.2.1. Personal Characteristics]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: characterizes the element in some sense, using any convenient classification scheme or typology. Sample values include: 1] practicing; 2] clandestine; 3] patrilineal; 4] matrilineal; 5] convert

rng:element.name: floruit
rng:element.a:documentation: (floruit) contains information about a person's period of activity. [14.3.2.1. Personal Characteristics]

rng:element.name: gender
rng:element.a:documentation: (gender) specifies the gender identity of a person, persona, or character. [14.3.2.1. Personal Characteristics]

rng:attribute.name: value
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies a coded value for gender identity.

rng:element.name: geo
rng:element.a:documentation: (geographical coordinates) contains any expression of a set of geographic coordinates, representing a point, line, or area on the surface of the earth in some notation. [14.3.4.1. Varieties of Location]

rng:element.name: langKnowledge
rng:element.a:documentation: (language knowledge) summarizes the state of a person's linguistic knowledge, either as prose or by a list of <langKnown> elements. [14.3.2.1. Personal Characteristics]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: characterizes the element in some sense, using any convenient classification scheme or typology. Sample values include: 1] listening; 2] speaking; 3] reading; 4] writing

rng:attribute.name: tags
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies one or more valid language tags for the languages specified.

rng:element.name: langKnown
rng:element.a:documentation: (language known) summarizes the state of a person's linguistic competence, i.e., knowledge of a single language. [16.2.2. The Participant Description]

rng:attribute.name: tag
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies a valid language tag for the language concerned.

rng:attribute.name: level
rng:attribute.a:documentation: a code indicating the person's level of knowledge for this language.

rng:element.name: listOrg
rng:element.a:documentation: (list of organizations) contains a list of elements, each of which provides information about an identifiable organization. [14.2.2. Organizational Names]

rng:element.name: listEvent
rng:element.a:documentation: (list of events) contains a list of descriptions, each of which provides information about an identifiable event. [14.3.1. Basic Principles]

rng:element.name: listPerson
rng:element.a:documentation: (list of persons) contains a list of descriptions, each of which provides information about an identifiable person or a group of people, for example the participants in a language interaction, or the people referred to in a historical source. [14.3.2. The Person Element 16.2. Contextual Information 2.4. The Profile Description 16.3.2. Declarable Elements]

rng:element.name: listPlace
rng:element.a:documentation: (list of places) contains a list of places, optionally followed by a list of relationships (other than containment) defined amongst them. [2.2.7. The Source Description 14.3.4. Places]

rng:element.name: listRelation
rng:element.a:documentation: provides information about relationships identified amongst people, places, and organizations, either informally as prose or as formally expressed relation links. [14.3.2.3. Personal Relationships]

rng:element.name: location
rng:element.a:documentation: (location) defines the location of a place as a set of geographical coordinates, in terms of other named geo-political entities, or as an address. [14.3.4. Places]

rng:element.name: nationality
rng:element.a:documentation: (nationality) contains an informal description of a person's present or past nationality or citizenship. [16.2.2. The Participant Description]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: characterizes the element in some sense, using any convenient classification scheme or typology. Sample values include: 1] birth; 2] naturalised; 3] self-assigned

rng:element.name: occupation
rng:element.a:documentation: (occupation) contains an informal description of a person's trade, profession or occupation. [16.2.2. The Participant Description]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: characterizes the element in some sense, using any convenient classification scheme or typology. Sample values include: 1] primary; 2] other; 3] paid; 4] unpaid

rng:attribute.name: scheme
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates the classification system or taxonomy in use, for example by supplying the identifier of a <taxonomy> element, or pointing to some other resource.

rng:attribute.name: code
rng:attribute.a:documentation: identifies an occupation code defined within the classification system or taxonomy defined by the @scheme attribute.

rng:element.name: org
rng:element.a:documentation: (organization) provides information about an identifiable organization such as a business, a tribe, or any other grouping of people. [14.3.3. Organizational Data]

rng:attribute.name: role
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies a primary role or classification for the organization.

rng:element.name: person
rng:element.a:documentation: (person) provides information about an identifiable individual, for example a participant in a language interaction, or a person referred to in a historical source. [14.3.2. The Person Element 16.2.2. The Participant Description]

rng:attribute.name: role
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies a primary role or classification for the person.

rng:attribute.name: sex
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the sex of the person.

rng:attribute.name: gender
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the gender of the person.

rng:attribute.name: age
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies an age group for the person.

rng:element.name: persona
rng:element.a:documentation: provides information about one of the personalities identified for a given individual, where an individual has multiple personalities. [14.3.2. The Person Element]

rng:attribute.name: role
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies a primary role or classification for the persona.

rng:attribute.name: sex
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the sex of the persona.

rng:attribute.name: gender
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the gender of the persona.

rng:attribute.name: age
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies an age group for the persona.

rng:element.name: personGrp
rng:element.a:documentation: (personal group) describes a group of individuals treated as a single person for analytic purposes. [16.2.2. The Participant Description]

rng:attribute.name: role
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the role of this group of participants in the interaction.

rng:attribute.name: sex
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the sex of the participant group.

rng:attribute.name: gender
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the gender of the participant group.

rng:attribute.name: age
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the age group of the participants.

rng:attribute.name: size
rng:attribute.a:documentation: describes informally the size or approximate size of the group for example by means of a number and an indication of accuracy e.g. approx 200.

rng:element.name: persPronouns
rng:element.a:documentation: (personal pronouns) indicates the personal pronouns used, or assumed to be used, by the individual being described. [14.3.2.1. Personal Characteristics]

rng:attribute.name: evidence
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (evidence) indicates support for the listed personal pronouns. Suggested values include: 1] conjecture (conjecture); 2] selfIdentification (self identification); 3] trustedThirdParty (trusted third party)

rng:choice.a:documentation: (conjecture) The given value was selected based on assumptions by someone besides the person to whom this pronoun applies. As a result, the value may be erroneous.
(self identification) The given value has been explicitly stated or confirmed by the person to whom this pronoun applies.
(trusted third party) The given value has been supplied by another individual trusted by the encoder to know the preferences of the person to whom this pronoun applies.

rng:attribute.name: value
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (value) supplies a regularized value for personal pronouns. Sample values include: 1] e (e); 2] he (he); 3] she (she); 4] they (they)

rng:element.name: place
rng:element.a:documentation: (place) contains data about a geographic location. [14.3.4. Places]

rng:element.name: population
rng:element.a:documentation: (population) contains information about the population of a place. [14.3.4.3. States, Traits, and Events]

rng:element.name: relation
rng:element.a:documentation: (relationship) describes any kind of relationship or linkage amongst a specified group of places, events, persons, objects or other items. [14.3.2.3. Personal Relationships]

sch:rule.sch:assert: One of the attributes @name, @ref or @key must be supplied.

sch:rule.sch:report: Only one of the attributes @active and @mutual may be supplied.
the attribute @passive may be supplied only if the attribute @active is supplied.

rng:attribute.name: name
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies a name for the kind of relationship of which this is an instance.

rng:attribute.name: active
rng:attribute.a:documentation: identifies the active participants in a non-mutual relationship, or all the participants in a mutual one.

rng:attribute.name: mutual
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies a list of participants amongst all of whom the relationship holds equally.

rng:attribute.name: passive
rng:attribute.a:documentation: identifies the passive participants in a non-mutual relationship.

rng:element.name: residence
rng:element.a:documentation: (residence) describes a person's present or past places of residence. [16.2.2. The Participant Description]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: characterizes the element in some sense, using any convenient classification scheme or typology. Sample values include: 1] primary; 2] secondary; 3] temporary; 4] permanent

rng:element.name: sex
rng:element.a:documentation: (sex) specifies the sex of an organism. [14.3.2.1. Personal Characteristics]

rng:attribute.name: value
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies a coded value for sex.

rng:element.name: socecStatus
rng:element.a:documentation: (socio-economic status) contains an informal description of a person's perceived social or economic status. [16.2.2. The Participant Description]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: characterizes the element in some sense, using any convenient classification scheme or typology. Sample values include: 1] atBirth; 2] atDeath; 3] dependent; 4] inherited; 5] independent

rng:attribute.name: scheme
rng:attribute.a:documentation: identifies the classification system or taxonomy in use, for example by pointing to a locally-defined <taxonomy> element or by supplying a URI for an externally-defined system.

rng:attribute.name: code
rng:attribute.a:documentation: identifies a status code defined within the classification system or taxonomy defined by the @scheme attribute.

rng:element.name: state
rng:element.a:documentation: (state) contains a description of some status or quality attributed to a person, place, or organization often at some specific time or for a specific date range. [14.3.1. Basic Principles 14.3.2.1. Personal Characteristics]

rng:element.name: terrain
