rng:element.a:documentation: (terrain) contains information about the physical terrain of a place. [14.3.4.3. States, Traits, and Events]

rng:element.name: trait
rng:element.a:documentation: (trait) contains a description of some status or quality attributed to a person, place, or organization typically, but not necessarily, independent of the volition or action of the holder and usually not at some specific time or for a specific date range. [14.3.1. Basic Principles 14.3.2.1. Personal Characteristics]

rng:element.name: objectName
rng:element.a:documentation: (name of an object) contains a proper noun or noun phrase used to refer to an object. [14.2.5. Object Names]

rng:element.name: object
rng:element.a:documentation: contains a description of a single identifiable physical object. [14.3.6. Objects]

rng:element.name: listObject
rng:element.a:documentation: (list of objects) contains a list of descriptions, each of which provides information about an identifiable physical object. [14.3.6. Objects]

rng:element.name: objectIdentifier
rng:element.a:documentation: (object identifier) groups one or more identifiers or pieces of locating information concerning a single object. [14.3.6. Objects]

rng:element.name: nym
rng:element.a:documentation: (canonical name) contains the definition for a canonical name or name component of any kind. [14.3.7. Names and Nyms]

rng:attribute.name: parts
rng:attribute.a:documentation: points to constituent nyms.

rng:element.name: listNym
rng:element.a:documentation: (list of canonical names) contains a list of nyms, that is, standardized names for any thing. [14.3.7. Names and Nyms]

rng:attribute.name: role
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (role) indicates the kind of information held in this cell or in each cell of this row. Suggested values include: 1] label; 2] data

rng:choice.a:documentation: labelling or descriptive information only.
data values.

rng:attribute.name: rows
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (rows) indicates the number of rows occupied by this cell or row.

rng:attribute.name: cols
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (columns) indicates the number of columns occupied by this cell or row.

rng:element.name: table
rng:element.a:documentation: (table) contains text displayed in tabular form, in rows and columns. [15.1.1. TEI Tables]

rng:attribute.name: rows
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (rows) indicates the number of rows in the table.

rng:attribute.name: cols
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (columns) indicates the number of columns in each row of the table.

rng:element.name: row
rng:element.a:documentation: (row) contains one row of a table. [15.1.1. TEI Tables]

rng:element.name: cell
rng:element.a:documentation: (cell) contains one cell of a table. [15.1.1. TEI Tables]

rng:element.name: formula
rng:element.a:documentation: (formula) contains a mathematical or other formula. [15.2. Formulæ and Mathematical Expressions]

rng:element.name: notatedMusic
rng:element.a:documentation: encodes the presence of music notation in a text. [15.3. Notated Music in Written Text]

rng:element.name: figure
rng:element.a:documentation: (figure) groups elements representing or containing graphic information such as an illustration, formula, or figure. [15.4. Specific Elements for Graphic Images]

rng:element.name: figDesc
rng:element.a:documentation: (description of figure) contains a brief prose description of the appearance or content of a graphic figure, for use when documenting an image without displaying it. [15.4. Specific Elements for Graphic Images]

rng:element.name: textDesc
rng:element.a:documentation: (text description) provides a description of a text in terms of its situational parameters. [16.2.1. The Text Description]

rng:element.name: particDesc
rng:element.a:documentation: (participation description) describes the identifiable speakers, voices, or other participants in any kind of text or other persons named or otherwise referred to in a text, edition, or metadata. [16.2. Contextual Information]

rng:element.name: settingDesc
rng:element.a:documentation: (setting description) describes the setting or settings within which a language interaction takes place, or other places otherwise referred to in a text, edition, or metadata. [16.2. Contextual Information 2.4. The Profile Description]

rng:element.name: channel
rng:element.a:documentation: (primary channel) describes the medium or channel by which a text is delivered or experienced. For a written text, this might be print, manuscript, email, etc.; for a spoken one, radio, telephone, face-to-face, etc. [16.2.1. The Text Description]

rng:attribute.name: mode
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the mode of this channel with respect to speech and writing.

rng:choice.a:documentation: (spoken)
(written)
(spoken to be written) e.g. dictation
(written to be spoken) e.g. a script
(mixed)
(unknown or inapplicable)

rng:element.name: constitution
rng:element.a:documentation: (constitution) describes the internal composition of a text or text sample, for example as fragmentary, complete, etc. [16.2.1. The Text Description]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies how the text was constituted.

rng:choice.a:documentation: a single complete text
a text made by combining several smaller items, each individually complete
(fragments) a text made by combining several smaller, not necessarily complete, items
composition unknown or unspecified

rng:element.name: derivation
rng:element.a:documentation: (derivation) describes the nature and extent of originality of this text. [16.2.1. The Text Description]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: categorizes the derivation of the text. Sample values include: 1] original; 2] revision; 3] translation; 4] abridgment; 5] plagiarism; 6] traditional

rng:element.name: domain
rng:element.a:documentation: (domain of use) describes the most important social context in which the text was realized or for which it is intended, for example private vs. public, education, religion, etc. [16.2.1. The Text Description]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: categorizes the domain of use. Sample values include: 1] art; 2] domestic; 3] religious; 4] business; 5] education (education); 6] govt (government); 7] public

rng:element.name: factuality
rng:element.a:documentation: (factuality) describes the extent to which the text may be regarded as imaginative or non-imaginative, that is, as describing a fictional or a non-fictional world. [16.2.1. The Text Description]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: categorizes the factuality of the text.

rng:choice.a:documentation: the text is to be regarded as entirely imaginative
the text is to be regarded as entirely informative or factual
the text contains a mixture of fact and fiction
the fiction/fact distinction is not regarded as helpful or appropriate to this text

rng:element.name: interaction
rng:element.a:documentation: (interaction) describes the extent, cardinality and nature of any interaction among those producing and experiencing the text, for example in the form of response or interjection, commentary, etc. [16.2.1. The Text Description]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the degree of interaction between active and passive participants in the text.

rng:choice.a:documentation: no interaction of any kind, e.g. a monologue
some degree of interaction, e.g. a monologue with set responses
complete interaction, e.g. a face to face conversation
this parameter is inappropriate or inapplicable in this case

rng:attribute.name: active
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the number of active participants (or addressors) producing parts of the text. Suggested values include: 1] singular; 2] plural; 3] corporate; 4] unknown

rng:choice.a:documentation: a single addressor
many addressors
a corporate addressor
number of addressors unknown or unspecifiable

rng:attribute.name: passive
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the number of passive participants (or addressees) to whom a text is directed or in whose presence it is created or performed. Suggested values include: 1] self; 2] single; 3] many; 4] group; 5] world

rng:choice.a:documentation: text is addressed to the originator e.g. a diary
text is addressed to one other person e.g. a personal letter
text is addressed to a countable number of others e.g. a conversation in which all participants are identified
text is addressed to an undefined but fixed number of participants e.g. a lecture
text is addressed to an undefined and indeterminately large number e.g. a published book

rng:element.name: preparedness
rng:element.a:documentation: (preparedness) describes the extent to which a text may be regarded as prepared or spontaneous. [16.2.1. The Text Description]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: a keyword characterizing the type of preparedness. Sample values include: 1] none; 2] scripted; 3] formulaic; 4] revised

rng:element.name: purpose
rng:element.a:documentation: characterizes a single purpose or communicative function of the text. [16.2.1. The Text Description]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies a particular kind of purpose. Suggested values include: 1] persuade; 2] express; 3] inform; 4] entertain

rng:choice.a:documentation: didactic, advertising, propaganda, etc.
self expression, confessional, etc.
convey information, educate, etc.
amuse, entertain, etc.

rng:attribute.name: degree
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the extent to which this purpose predominates.

rng:element.name: setting
rng:element.a:documentation: describes one particular setting in which a language interaction takes place. [16.2.3. The Setting Description]

rng:element.name: locale
rng:element.a:documentation: contains a brief informal description of the kind of place concerned, for example: a room, a restaurant, a park bench, etc. [16.2.3. The Setting Description]

rng:element.name: activity
rng:element.a:documentation: (activity) contains a brief informal description of what a participant in a language interaction is doing other than speaking, if anything. [16.2.3. The Setting Description]

rng:attribute.name: corresp
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (corresponds) points to elements that correspond to the current element in some way.

rng:attribute.name: synch
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (synchronous) points to elements that are synchronous with the current element.

rng:attribute.name: sameAs
rng:attribute.a:documentation: points to an element that is the same as the current element.

rng:attribute.name: copyOf
rng:attribute.a:documentation: points to an element of which the current element is a copy.

rng:attribute.name: next
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (next) points to the next element of a virtual aggregate of which the current element is part.

rng:attribute.name: prev
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (previous) points to the previous element of a virtual aggregate of which the current element is part.

rng:attribute.name: exclude
rng:attribute.a:documentation: points to elements that are in exclusive alternation with the current element.

rng:attribute.name: select
rng:attribute.a:documentation: selects one or more alternants; if one alternant is selected, the ambiguity or uncertainty is marked as resolved. If more than one alternant is selected, the degree of ambiguity or uncertainty is marked as reduced by the number of alternants not selected.

rng:element.name: link
rng:element.a:documentation: (link) defines an association or hypertextual link among elements or passages, of some type not more precisely specifiable by other elements. [17.1. Links]

sch:rule.sch:assert: You must supply at least two values for @target on <>.

rng:element.name: linkGrp
rng:element.a:documentation: (link group) defines a collection of associations or hypertextual links. [17.1. Links]

rng:element.name: ab
rng:element.a:documentation: (anonymous block) contains any component-level unit of text, acting as a container for phrase or inter level elements analogous to, but without the same constraints as, a paragraph. [17.3. Blocks, Segments, and Anchors]

sch:rule.sch:assert:
Abstract model violation: Metrical lines ( elements) may not contain higher-level divisions such as

or , unless is a child of

rng:element.name: anchor
rng:element.a:documentation: (anchor point) attaches an identifier to a point within a text, whether or not it corresponds with a textual element. [8.4.2. Synchronization and Overlap 17.5. Correspondence and Alignment]

rng:element.name: seg
rng:element.a:documentation: (arbitrary segment) represents any segmentation of text below the chunk level. [17.3. Blocks, Segments, and Anchors 6.2. Components of the Verse Line 7.2.6. Speech Contents]

rng:element.name: when
rng:element.a:documentation: indicates a point in time either relative to other elements in the same timeline tag, or absolutely. [17.4.2. Placing Synchronous Events in Time]

rng:attribute.name: absolute
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies an absolute value for the time.

rng:attribute.name: unit
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the unit of time in which the @interval value is expressed, if this is not inherited from the parent <timeline>. Suggested values include: 1] d (days); 2] h (hours); 3] min (minutes); 4] s (seconds); 5] ms (milliseconds)

rng:choice.a:documentation: (days)
(hours)
(minutes)
(seconds)
(milliseconds)

rng:attribute.name: interval
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies a time interval either as a number or as one of the keywords defined by the datatype teidata.interval.

rng:attribute.name: since
rng:attribute.a:documentation: identifies the reference point for determining the time of the current <when> element, which is obtained by adding the interval to the time of the reference point.

rng:element.name: timeline
rng:element.a:documentation: (timeline) provides a set of ordered points in time which can be linked to elements of a spoken text to create a temporal alignment of that text. [17.4.2. Placing Synchronous Events in Time]

rng:attribute.name: origin
rng:attribute.a:documentation: designates the origin of the timeline, i.e. the time at which it begins.

rng:attribute.name: unit
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the unit of time corresponding to the @interval value of the timeline or of its constituent points in time. Suggested values include: 1] d (days); 2] h (hours); 3] min (minutes); 4] s (seconds); 5] ms (milliseconds)

rng:choice.a:documentation: (days)
(hours)
(minutes)
(seconds)
(milliseconds)

rng:attribute.name: interval
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies a time interval either as a positive integral value or using one of a set of predefined codes.

rng:element.name: join
rng:element.a:documentation: (join) identifies a possibly fragmented segment of text, by pointing at the possibly discontiguous elements which compose it. [17.7. Aggregation]

sch:rule.sch:assert: You must supply at least two values for @target on <>.

rng:attribute.name: result
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the name of an element which this aggregation may be understood to represent.

rng:attribute.name: scope
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates whether the targets to be joined include the entire element indicated (the entire subtree including its root), or just the children of the target (the branches of the subtree).

rng:choice.a:documentation: the rooted subtrees indicated by the @target attribute are joined, each subtree become a child of the virtual element created by the join
the children of the subtrees indicated by the @target attribute become the children of the virtual element (i.e. the roots of the subtrees are discarded)

rng:element.name: joinGrp
rng:element.a:documentation: (join group) groups a collection of <join> elements and possibly pointers. [17.7. Aggregation]

rng:attribute.name: result
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies the default value for the @result on each <join> included within the group.

rng:element.name: alt
rng:element.a:documentation: (alternation) identifies an alternation or a set of choices among elements or passages. [17.8. Alternation]

rng:attribute.name: target
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the destination of the reference by supplying one or more URI References.

rng:attribute.name: mode
rng:attribute.a:documentation: states whether the alternations gathered in this collection are exclusive or inclusive.

rng:choice.a:documentation: (exclusive) indicates that the alternation is exclusive, i.e. that at most one of the alternatives occurs.
(inclusive) indicates that the alternation is not exclusive, i.e. that one or more of the alternatives occur.

rng:attribute.name: weights
rng:attribute.a:documentation: If @mode is excl, each weight states the probability that the corresponding alternative occurs. If @mode is incl each weight states the probability that the corresponding alternative occurs given that at least one of the other alternatives occurs.

rng:element.name: altGrp
rng:element.a:documentation: (alternation group) groups a collection of <alt> elements and possibly pointers. [17.8. Alternation]

rng:attribute.name: mode
rng:attribute.a:documentation: states whether the alternations gathered in this collection are exclusive or inclusive.

rng:choice.a:documentation: (exclusive) indicates that the alternation is exclusive, i.e. that at most one of the alternatives occurs.
(inclusive) indicates that the alternation is not exclusive, i.e. that one or more of the alternatives occur.

rng:element.name: standOff
rng:element.a:documentation: functions as a container element for linked data, contextual information, and stand-off annotations embedded in a TEI document. [17.10. The standOff Container]

rng:element.name: listAnnotation
rng:element.a:documentation: contains a list of annotations, typically encoded as <annotation>, <annotationBlock>, or <note>, possibly organized with nested <listAnnotation> elements. [17.10. The standOff Container]

rng:element.name: annotation
rng:element.a:documentation: represents an annotation following the Web Annotation Data Model. [17.10. The standOff Container]

rng:attribute.name: xml:id
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (identifier) provides a unique identifier for the element bearing the attribute.

rng:attribute.name: target
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the destination of the reference by supplying one or more URI References.

rng:choice.a:documentation: intent is to assess the target resource in some way, rather than simply make a comment about it
intent is to create a bookmark to the target or part thereof
intent is to classify the target in some way
intent is to comment about the target
intent is to describe the target, rather than (for example) comment on it
intent is to request an edit or a change to the target resource
intent is to highlight the target resource or a segment thereof
intent is to assign an identity to the target
intent is to link to a resource related to the target
intent is to assign some value or quality to the target
intent is to ask a question about the target
intent is to reply to a previous statement, either an annotation or another resource
intent is to associate a tag with the target

rng:element.name: fsdDecl
rng:element.a:documentation: (feature system declaration) provides a feature system declaration comprising one or more feature structure declarations or feature structure declaration links. [19.11. Feature System Declaration]

rng:element.name: fsDecl
rng:element.a:documentation: (feature structure declaration) declares one type of feature structure. [19.11. Feature System Declaration]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: gives a name for the type of feature structure being declared.

rng:attribute.name: baseTypes
rng:attribute.a:documentation: gives the name of one or more typed feature structures from which this type inherits feature specifications and constraints; if this type includes a feature specification with the same name as that of any of those specified by this attribute, or if more than one specification of the same name is inherited, then the set of possible values is defined by unification. Similarly, the set of constraints applicable is derived by combining those specified explicitly within this element with those implied by the @baseTypes attribute. When no @baseTypes attribute is specified, no feature specification or constraint is inherited.

rng:element.name: fsDescr
rng:element.a:documentation: (feature system description (in FSD)) describes in prose what is represented by the type of feature structure declared in the enclosing fsDecl. [19.11. Feature System Declaration]

rng:element.name: fsdLink
rng:element.a:documentation: (feature structure declaration link) associates the name of a typed feature structure with a feature structure declaration for it. [19.11. Feature System Declaration]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: identifies the type of feature structure to be documented; this will be the value of the @type attribute on at least one feature structure.

rng:attribute.name: target
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies a pointer to a feature structure declaration (<fsDecl>) element within the current document or elsewhere.

rng:element.name: fDecl
rng:element.a:documentation: (feature declaration) declares a single feature, specifying its name, organization, range of allowed values, and optionally its default value. [19.11. Feature System Declaration]

rng:attribute.name: name
rng:attribute.a:documentation: a single word which follows the rules defining a legal XML name (see ), indicating the name of the feature being declared; matches the @name attribute of <f> elements in the text.

rng:attribute.name: optional
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates whether or not the value of this feature may be present.

rng:element.name: fDescr
rng:element.a:documentation: (feature description (in FSD)) describes in prose what is represented by the feature being declared and its values. [19.11. Feature System Declaration]

rng:element.name: vRange
rng:element.a:documentation: (value range) defines the range of allowed values for a feature, in the form of an <fs>, <vAlt>, or primitive value; for the value of an <f> to be valid, it must be subsumed by the specified range; if the <f> contains multiple values (as sanctioned by the @org attribute), then each value must be subsumed by the <vRange>. [19.11. Feature System Declaration]

rng:element.name: vDefault
rng:element.a:documentation: (value default) declares the default value to be supplied when a feature structure does not contain an instance of <f> for this name; if unconditional, it is specified as one (or, depending on the value of the @org attribute of the enclosing <fDecl>) more <fs> elements or primitive values; if conditional, it is specified as one or more <if> elements; if no default is specified, or no condition matches, the value none is assumed. [19.11. Feature System Declaration]

rng:element.name: if
rng:element.a:documentation: defines a conditional default value for a feature; the condition is specified as a feature structure, and is met if it subsumes the feature structure in the text for which a default value is sought. [19.11. Feature System Declaration]

rng:element.name: then
rng:element.a:documentation: separates the condition from the default in an <if>, or the antecedent and the consequent in a <cond> element. [19.11. Feature System Declaration]

rng:element.name: fsConstraints
rng:element.a:documentation: (feature-structure constraints) specifies constraints on the content of valid feature structures. [19.11. Feature System Declaration]

rng:element.name: cond
rng:element.a:documentation: (conditional feature-structure constraint) defines a conditional feature-structure constraint; the consequent and the antecedent are specified as feature structures or feature-structure collections; the constraint is satisfied if both the antecedent and the consequent subsume a given feature structure, or if the antecedent does not. [19.11. Feature System Declaration]

rng:element.name: bicond
rng:element.a:documentation: (bi-conditional feature-structure constraint) defines a biconditional feature-structure constraint; both consequent and antecedent are specified as feature structures or groups of feature structures; the constraint is satisfied if both subsume a given feature structure, or if both do not. [19.11. Feature System Declaration]

rng:element.name: iff
rng:element.a:documentation: (if and only if) separates the condition from the consequence in a <bicond> element. [19.11. Feature System Declaration]

rng:element.name: fs
rng:element.a:documentation: (feature structure) represents a feature structure, that is, a collection of feature-value pairs organized as a structural unit. [19.2. Elementary Feature Structures and the Binary Feature Value]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the type of the feature structure.

rng:attribute.name: feats
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (features) references the feature-value specifications making up this feature structure.

rng:element.name: f
rng:element.a:documentation: (feature) represents a feature value specification, that is, the association of a name with a value of any of several different types. [19.2. Elementary Feature Structures and the Binary Feature Value]

rng:attribute.name: name
rng:attribute.a:documentation: a single word which follows the rules defining a legal XML name (see ), providing a name for the feature.

rng:attribute.name: fVal
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (feature value) references any element which can be used to represent the value of a feature.

rng:element.name: binary
rng:element.a:documentation: (binary value) represents the value part of a feature-value specification which can contain either of exactly two possible values. [19.2. Elementary Feature Structures and the Binary Feature Value]

rng:attribute.name: value
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies a binary value.

rng:element.name: symbol
rng:element.a:documentation: (symbolic value) represents the value part of a feature-value specification which contains one of a finite list of symbols. [19.3. Other Atomic Feature Values]

rng:attribute.name: value
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies a symbolic value for the feature, one of a finite list that may be specified in a feature declaration.

rng:element.name: numeric
rng:element.a:documentation: (numeric value) represents the value part of a feature-value specification which contains a numeric value or range. [19.3. Other Atomic Feature Values]

rng:attribute.name: value
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies a lower bound for the numeric value represented, and also (if @max is not supplied) its upper bound.

rng:attribute.name: max
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies an upper bound for the numeric value represented.

rng:attribute.name: trunc
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies whether the value represented should be truncated to give an integer value.

rng:element.name: string
rng:element.a:documentation: (string value) represents the value part of a feature-value specification which contains a string. [19.3. Other Atomic Feature Values]

rng:element.name: vLabel
rng:element.a:documentation: (value label) represents the value part of a feature-value specification which appears at more than one point in a feature structure. [19.6. Re-entrant Feature Structures]

rng:attribute.name: name
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies a name identifying the sharing point.

rng:element.name: vColl
rng:element.a:documentation: (collection of values) represents the value part of a feature-value specification which contains multiple values organized as a set, bag, or list. [19.7. Collections as Complex Feature Values]

rng:attribute.name: org
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (organization) indicates organization of given value or values as set, bag or list.

rng:choice.a:documentation: indicates that the given values are organized as a set.
indicates that the given values are organized as a bag (multiset).
indicates that the given values are organized as a list.

rng:element.name: default
rng:element.a:documentation: (default feature value) represents the value part of a feature-value specification which contains a defaulted value. [19.9. Default Values]

rng:element.name: vAlt
rng:element.a:documentation: (value alternation) represents the value part of a feature-value specification which contains a set of values, only one of which can be valid. [19.8.1. Alternation]

rng:element.name: vNot
rng:element.a:documentation: (value negation) represents a feature value which is the negation of its content. [19.8.2. Negation]

rng:element.name: vMerge
rng:element.a:documentation: (merged collection of values) represents a feature value which is the result of merging together the feature values contained by its children, using the organization specified by the @org attribute. [19.8.3. Collection of Values]

rng:attribute.name: org
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates the organization of the resulting merged values as set, bag or list.

rng:choice.a:documentation: indicates that the resulting values are organized as a set.
indicates that the resulting values are organized as a bag (multiset).
indicates that the resulting values are organized as a list.

rng:element.name: fLib
rng:element.a:documentation: (feature library) assembles a library of <f> (feature) elements. [19.4. Feature Libraries and Feature-Value Libraries]

rng:element.name: fvLib
rng:element.a:documentation: (feature-value library) assembles a library of reusable feature value elements (including complete feature structures). [19.4. Feature Libraries and Feature-Value Libraries]

rng:element.name: graph
rng:element.a:documentation: (graph) encodes a graph, which is a collection of nodes, and arcs which connect the nodes. [20.1. Graphs and Digraphs]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: describes the type of graph. Suggested values include: 1] undirected; 2] directed; 3] transitionNetwork; 4] transducer

rng:choice.a:documentation: undirected graph
directed graph
a directed graph with distinguished initial and final nodes
a transition network with up to two labels on each arc

rng:attribute.name: order
rng:attribute.a:documentation: states the order of the graph, i.e., the number of its nodes.

rng:attribute.name: size
rng:attribute.a:documentation: states the size of the graph, i.e., the number of its arcs.

rng:element.name: node
rng:element.a:documentation: (node) encodes a node, a possibly labeled point in a graph. [20.1. Graphs and Digraphs]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: provides a type for a node. Suggested values include: 1] initial; 2] final

rng:choice.a:documentation: initial node in a transition network
final node in a transition network

rng:attribute.name: value
rng:attribute.a:documentation: provides the value of a node, which is a feature structure or other analytic element.

rng:attribute.name: adjTo
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (adjacent to) gives the identifiers of the nodes which are adjacent to the current node.

rng:attribute.name: adjFrom
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (adjacent from) gives the identifiers of the nodes which are adjacent from the current node.

rng:attribute.name: adj
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (adjacent) gives the identifiers of the nodes which are both adjacent to and adjacent from the current node.

rng:attribute.name: inDegree
rng:attribute.a:documentation: gives the in degree of the node, the number of nodes which are adjacent from the given node.

rng:attribute.name: outDegree
rng:attribute.a:documentation: gives the out degree of the node, the number of nodes which are adjacent to the given node.

rng:attribute.name: degree
rng:attribute.a:documentation: gives the degree of the node, the number of arcs with which the node is incident.

rng:element.name: arc
rng:element.a:documentation: (arc) encodes an arc, the connection from one node to another in a graph. [20.1. Graphs and Digraphs]

rng:attribute.name: from
rng:attribute.a:documentation: gives the identifier of the node which is adjacent from this arc.

rng:attribute.name: to
rng:attribute.a:documentation: gives the identifier of the node which is adjacent to this arc.

rng:element.name: tree
rng:element.a:documentation: (tree) encodes a tree, which is made up of a root, internal nodes, leaves, and arcs from root to leaves. [20.2. Trees]

rng:attribute.name: arity
rng:attribute.a:documentation: gives the maximum number of children of the root and internal nodes of the tree.

rng:attribute.name: ord
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (ordered) indicates whether or not the tree is ordered, or if it is partially ordered.

rng:choice.a:documentation: indicates that all of the branching nodes of the tree are ordered.
indicates that some of the branching nodes of the tree are ordered and some are unordered.
indicates that all of the branching nodes of the tree are unordered.

rng:attribute.name: order
rng:attribute.a:documentation: gives the order of the tree, i.e., the number of its nodes.

rng:element.name: root
rng:element.a:documentation: (root node) represents the root node of a tree. [20.2. Trees]

rng:attribute.name: value
rng:attribute.a:documentation: identifies the root node of the network by pointing to a feature structure or other analytic element.

rng:attribute.name: children
rng:attribute.a:documentation: identifies the elements which are the children of the root node.

rng:attribute.name: ord
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (ordered) indicates whether or not the root is ordered.

rng:attribute.name: outDegree
rng:attribute.a:documentation: gives the out degree of the root, the number of its children.

rng:element.name: iNode
rng:element.a:documentation: (intermediate (or internal) node) represents an intermediate (or internal) node of a tree. [20.2. Trees]

rng:attribute.name: value
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates an intermediate node, which is a feature structure or other analytic element.

rng:attribute.name: children
rng:attribute.a:documentation: provides a list of identifiers of the elements which are the children of the intermediate node.

rng:attribute.name: parent
rng:attribute.a:documentation: provides the identifier of the element which is the parent of this node.

rng:attribute.name: ord
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (ordered) indicates whether or not the internal node is ordered.

rng:attribute.name: follow
rng:attribute.a:documentation: provides the identifier of an element which this node follows.

rng:attribute.name: outDegree
rng:attribute.a:documentation: gives the out degree of an intermediate node, the number of its children.

rng:element.name: leaf
rng:element.a:documentation: (leaf) encodes the leaves (terminal nodes) of a tree. [20.2. Trees]

rng:attribute.name: value
rng:attribute.a:documentation: provides a pointer to a feature structure or other analytic element.

rng:attribute.name: parent
rng:attribute.a:documentation: provides the identifier of parent of a leaf.

rng:attribute.name: follow
rng:attribute.a:documentation: provides an identifier of an element which this leaf follows.

rng:element.name: eTree
rng:element.a:documentation: (embedding tree) provides an alternative to the <tree> element for representing ordered rooted tree structures. [20.3. Another Tree Notation]

rng:attribute.name: value
rng:attribute.a:documentation: provides the value of an embedding tree, which is a feature structure or other analytic element.

rng:element.name: triangle
rng:element.a:documentation: (underspecified embedding tree, so called because of its characteristic shape when drawn) provides for an underspecified <eTree>, that is, an <eTree> with information left out. [20.3. Another Tree Notation]

rng:attribute.name: value
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies a value for the triangle, in the form of the identifier of a feature structure or other analytic element.

rng:element.name: eLeaf
rng:element.a:documentation: (leaf or terminal node of an embedding tree) provides explicitly for a leaf of an embedding tree, which may also be encoded with the <eTree> element. [20.3. Another Tree Notation]

rng:attribute.name: value
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates the value of an embedding leaf, which is a feature structure or other analytic element.

rng:element.name: forest
rng:element.a:documentation: (forest) provides for groups of rooted trees. [20.3. Another Tree Notation]

rng:element.name: listForest
rng:element.a:documentation: provides for lists of forests. [20.3. Another Tree Notation]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: identifies the type of the forest group.

rng:element.name: precision
rng:element.a:documentation: indicates the numerical accuracy or precision associated with some aspect of the text markup. [22.2. Indications of Precision]

rng:attribute.name: precision
rng:attribute.a:documentation: characterizes the precision of the element or attribute pointed to by the <precision> element.

rng:attribute.name: stdDeviation
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies a standard deviation associated with the value in question.

rng:element.name: certainty
rng:element.a:documentation: indicates the degree of certainty associated with some aspect of the text markup. [22.1.2. Structured Indications of Uncertainty]

rng:attribute.name: cert
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (certainty) signifies the degree of certainty associated with the object pointed to by the <certainty> element.

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: characterizes the element in some sense, using any convenient classification scheme or typology; sample categorization of annotations of uncertainty might use following values: Sample values include: 1] ignorance; 2] incompleteness; 3] credibility; 4] imprecision

rng:attribute.name: locus
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates more exactly the aspect concerning which certainty is being expressed: specifically, whether the markup is correctly located, whether the correct element or attribute name has been used, or whether the content of the element or attribute is correct, etc.

rng:choice.a:documentation: uncertainty concerns whether the name of the element or attribute used is correctly applied.
uncertainty concerns whether the start of the element is correctly identified.
uncertainty concerns whether the end of the element is correctly identified.
uncertainty concerns both the start and the end of the element.
uncertainty concerns the content (for an element) or the value (for an attribute)

rng:attribute.name: assertedValue
rng:attribute.a:documentation: provides an alternative value for the aspect of the markup in question—an alternative generic identifier, transcription, or attribute value, or the identifier of an <anchor> element (to indicate an alternative starting or ending location). If an @assertedValue is given, the confidence level specified by @degree applies to the alternative markup specified by @assertedValue; if none is given, it applies to the markup in the text.

rng:attribute.name: given
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates one or more element(s) characterizing the conditions which are assumed in the assignment of a degree of confidence.

rng:attribute.name: degree
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates the degree of confidence assigned to the aspect of the markup named by the @locus attribute.

rng:element.name: respons
rng:element.a:documentation: (responsibility) identifies the individual(s) responsible for some aspect of the content or markup of particular element(s). [22.3. Attribution of Responsibility]

rng:attribute.name: locus
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates the specific aspect of the encoding (markup or content) for which responsibility is being assigned.

rng:choice.a:documentation: responsibility is being assigned concerning the name of the element or attribute used.
responsibility is being assigned concerning the start of the element concerned.
responsibility is being assigned concerning the end of the element concerned.
responsibility is being assigned concerning the location of the element concerned.
responsibility is being assigned concerning the content (for an element) or the value (for an attribute)

rng:attribute.name: versionDate
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the date on which the source text was extracted and sent to the translator

rng:attribute.name: predicate
rng:attribute.a:documentation: the condition under which the element bearing this attribute applies, given as an XPath predicate expression.

rng:attribute.name: minOccurs
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (minimum number of occurrences) indicates the smallest number of times this component may occur.

rng:attribute.name: maxOccurs
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (maximum number of occurrences) indicates the largest number of times this component may occur.

sch:let.name: max
sch:let.value: if ( normalize-space( @maxOccurs ) eq 'unbounded') then -1 else @maxOccurs cast as xs:integer

sch:rule.sch:assert: @maxOccurs should be greater than or equal to @minOccurs.
When @maxOccurs is not specified, @minOccurs must be 0 or 1.

rng:attribute.name: mode
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies the effect of this declaration on its parent object.

rng:choice.a:documentation: this declaration is part of the current definitions.
the object with the same identifier (and namespace in the case of an element or attribute) as the current one is no longer part of the current definitions
this declaration changes the object of the same identifier (and namespace in the case of an element or attribute) in the current definition
this declaration replaces the object with the same identifier (and namespace in the case of an element or attribute) in the current definition.

rng:attribute.name: ident
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies the identifier by which this element may be referenced.

rng:attribute.name: predeclare
rng:attribute.a:documentation: says whether this object should be predeclared in the tei infrastructure module.

rng:attribute.name: module
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies a name for the module in which this object is to be declared.

sch:rule.context: ( tei:elementSpec[@module] | tei:classSpec[@module] | tei:macroSpec[@module] )[ ( ancestor::tei:schemaSpec | ancestor::tei:TEI | ancestor::tei:teiCorpus ) and ( //tei:moduleSpec | //tei:moduleRef ) ]
sch:rule.sch:assert: Specification : the value of the module attribute ("") should correspond to an existing module, via a moduleSpec or moduleRef.

rng:attribute.name: validUntil
rng:attribute.a:documentation: provides a date before which the construct being defined will not be removed.

sch:let.name: me_phrase
sch:let.value: if (@ident) then concat('The ', @ident ) else concat('This ', local-name(.), ' of ', ancestor::tei:*[@ident][1]/@ident )

sch:value-of.select: concat( $me_phrase, ' construct is outdated (as of ', @validUntil, '); ODD processors may ignore it, and its use is no longer supported.' )

sch:rule.context: tei:*[@validUntil][ not( self::tei:valDesc | self::tei:valList | self::tei:defaultVal | self::tei:remarks )]
sch:rule.sch:assert: A deprecated construct should include, whenever possible, an explanation, but this does not have a child <desc type="deprecationInfo">.

rng:attribute.name: ns
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (namespace) specifies the namespace to which the element(s) being specified belongs.

rng:element.name: att
rng:element.a:documentation: (attribute) contains the name of an attribute appearing within running text. [23. Documentation Elements]

rng:attribute.name: scheme
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (scheme) supplies an identifier for the scheme in which this name is defined. Sample values include: 1] TEI (Text Encoding Initiative); 2] DBK (Docbook); 3] XX (unknown); 4] imaginary (imaginary); 5] XHTML (XHTML); 6] XML (XML); 7] XI (XI)

rng:element.name: code
rng:element.a:documentation: contains literal code from some formal language such as a programming language. [23.1.1. Phrase Level Terms]

rng:attribute.name: lang
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (formal language) a name identifying the formal language in which the code is expressed.

rng:element.name: eg
rng:element.a:documentation: (example) contains any kind of illustrative example. [23.5. Element Specifications 23.5.3. Attribute List Specification]

rng:element.name: egXML
rng:element.a:documentation: (example of XML) a single XML fragment demonstrating the use of some XML, such as elements, attributes, or processing instructions, etc., in which the <egXML> element functions as the root element. [23.1.1. Phrase Level Terms]

rng:attribute.name: valid
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates the intended validity of the example with respect to a schema.

rng:choice.a:documentation: the example is intended to be fully valid, assuming that its root element, or a provided root element, could have been used as a possible root element in the schema concerned.

the example could be transformed into a valid document by inserting any number of valid attributes and child elements anywhere within it; or it is valid against a version of the schema concerned in which the provision of character data, list, element, or attribute values has been made optional.
the example is not intended to be valid, and contains deliberate errors.

rng:element.name: gi
rng:element.a:documentation: (element name) contains the name (generic identifier) of an element. [23. Documentation Elements 23.5. Element Specifications]

rng:attribute.name: scheme
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies the name of the scheme in which this name is defined. Sample values include: 1] TEI; 2] DBK (docbook); 3] XX (unknown); 4] Schematron; 5] HTML

rng:element.name: ident
rng:element.a:documentation: (identifier) contains an identifier or name for an object of some kind in a formal language. <ident> is used for tokens such as variable names, class names, type names, function names etc. in formal programming languages. [23.1.1. Phrase Level Terms]

rng:element.name: tag
rng:element.a:documentation: (tag) contains text of a complete start- or end-tag, possibly including attribute specifications, but excluding the opening and closing markup delimiter characters. [23. Documentation Elements]

rng:attribute.name: type
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates the type of XML tag intended.

rng:choice.a:documentation: a start-tag, with delimiters < and > is intended
an end-tag, with delimiters </ and > is intended
an empty tag, with delimiters < and /> is intended
a pi (processing instruction), with delimiters <? and ?> is intended
a comment, with delimiters <!-- and --> is intended
a marked-section, with delimiters <[CDATA[ and ]]> is intended

rng:attribute.name: scheme
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies the name of the schema in which this tag is defined. Sample values include: 1] TEI (text encoding initiative); 2] DBK (docbook); 3] XX (unknown); 4] Schematron; 5] HTML

rng:element.name: val
rng:element.a:documentation: (value) contains a single attribute value. [23. Documentation Elements 23.5.3. Attribute List Specification]

rng:element.name: specList
rng:element.a:documentation: (specification list) marks where a list of descriptions is to be inserted into the prose documentation. [23.1.2. Element and Attribute Descriptions]

rng:element.name: specDesc
rng:element.a:documentation: (specification description) indicates that a description of the specified element, class, or macro should be included at this point within a document. [23.1.2. Element and Attribute Descriptions]

rng:attribute.name: key
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (identifier) supplies the identifier of the documentary element or class for which a description is to be obtained.

rng:attribute.name: atts
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (attributes) supplies attribute names for which descriptions should additionally be obtained.

rng:element.name: classRef
rng:element.a:documentation: points to the specification for an attribute or model class which is to be included in a schema. [23.6. Class Specifications]

rng:attribute.name: key
rng:attribute.a:documentation: the identifier used for the required class within the source indicated.

rng:attribute.name: expand
rng:attribute.a:documentation: indicates how references to this class within a content model should be interpreted.

rng:choice.a:documentation: any one member of the class may appear
a single occurrence of all members of the class may appear in sequence
a single occurrence of one or more members of the class may appear in sequence
one or more occurrences of one or more members of the class may appear in sequence.
one or more occurrences of all members of the class may appear in sequence

rng:attribute.name: include
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies a list of class members which are to be included in the schema being defined.

rng:attribute.name: except
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies a list of class members which are to be excluded from the schema being defined.

rng:element.name: elementRef
rng:element.a:documentation: points to the specification for some element which is to be included in a schema. [23.2. Modules and Schemas]

sch:rule.sch:report: An element reference is not repeatable when part of a schema specification (and thus this <elementRef> should not have @minOccurs or @maxOccurs).
An element reference within a content model must refer to a locally defined element specification (and thus this <elementRef> should not have @source).

rng:attribute.name: key
rng:attribute.a:documentation: the identifier used for the required element within the source indicated.

rng:element.name: macroRef
rng:element.a:documentation: points to the specification for some pattern which is to be included in a schema. [23.7. Macro Specifications]

rng:attribute.name: key
rng:attribute.a:documentation: the identifier used for the required pattern within the source indicated.

rng:element.name: moduleRef
rng:element.a:documentation: (module reference) references a module which is to be incorporated into a schema. [23.2. Modules and Schemas]

sch:rule.sch:report: Child elements of <> are only allowed when an external module is being loaded.

rng:attribute.name: prefix
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies a default prefix which will be prepended to all patterns from the imported module.

sch:rule.sch:report: The @prefix attribute of <> should not match that of any other element (it would defeat the purpose).
It is an error to supply both the @include and @except attributes.

rng:attribute.name: include
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies a list of the elements which are to be copied from the specified module into the schema being defined.

rng:attribute.name: except
rng:attribute.a:documentation: supplies a list of the elements which are not to be copied from the specified module into the schema being defined.

rng:attribute.name: key
rng:attribute.a:documentation: the name of a TEI module

rng:attribute.name: url
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (uniform resource locator) refers to a non-TEI module of RELAX NG code by external location

rng:element.name: moduleSpec
rng:element.a:documentation: (module specification) documents the structure, content, and purpose of a single module, i.e. a named and externally visible group of declarations. [23.2. Modules and Schemas]

rng:element.name: schemaSpec
rng:element.a:documentation: (schema specification) generates a TEI-conformant schema and documentation for it. [2.3. The Encoding Description 23.2. Modules and Schemas 24.5.1. Making a Unified ODD]

rng:attribute.name: start
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies entry points to the schema, i.e. which patterns may be used as the root of documents conforming to it.

rng:attribute.name: prefix
rng:attribute.a:documentation: specifies a default prefix which will be prepended to all patterns relating to TEI elements, unless otherwise stated.

rng:attribute.name: targetLang
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (target language) specifies which language to use when creating the objects in a schema if names for elements or attributes are available in more than one language.

rng:attribute.name: docLang
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (documentation language) specifies which languages to use when creating documentation if the description for an element, attribute, class or macro is available in more than one language.

rng:attribute.name: defaultExceptions
rng:attribute.a:documentation: (default namespace exclusions) provides a list of namespaces and/or prefixed element names to be excluded by default from anyName in RELAX NG schemas.

rng:element.name: specGrp
rng:element.a:documentation: (specification group) contains any convenient grouping of specifications for use within the current module. [23.2. Modules and Schemas]

rng:element.name: specGrpRef
rng:element.a:documentation: (reference to a specification group) indicates that the declarations contained by the <specGrp> referenced should be inserted at this point. [23.2. Modules and Schemas]

rng:attribute.name: target
rng:attribute.a:documentation: points at the specification group which logically belongs here.
